name: Shared kit and co-op portal
replaces: The services every platform rebuilds or rents: sign-in and identity services (such as Auth0 and Okta), map and routing services (such as Google Maps Platform and Mapbox), chat, call and notification services (such as Twilio, SendGrid, Firebase and Zoom), e-signature services (such as DocuSign), trust and safety tools, voting tools (such as Loomio and Decidim), open budget tools (such as Open Collective) and back-office systems, plus the member register and portal a co-op would otherwise run by hand.
summary: One set of libraries and services every Spareware app is built on: accounts, payments and payouts, tax, matching, maps, messaging, trust and safety, worker law, property records, member voting, the open cost ledger, sync and history, plugins and AI access, and it maps the shared engines the programs use. It also runs the member portal, where people join for free, vote and check the costs.

areas.name: Accounts and sign-in
areas.summary: One Spareware login for every app: signing up, signing in safely, getting back into a lost account, devices, roles, teams, and the sign-in service other apps and AI agents can use. Built as svc-accounts.

features.name: Sign up once for every app
features.does: Create one Spareware account with an email or phone number and use it in every app.

parts.name: Account service
parts.what: Stores accounts, verified emails and phones, and the apps each person uses, with every change an operation.

parts.name: Sign-up flow
parts.what: A short sign-up in every app that asks only what that app needs and records which terms were accepted.

parts.name: Email and phone checks
parts.what: Confirms an email or phone number with a one-time code or link.

parts.name: Sign-up abuse protection
parts.what: Rules for slowing mass sign-ups, set on the shared limiter, with privacy-friendly checks and never an outside tracker.

parts.name: Minimum age at sign-up
parts.what: The youngest age each app accepts, and how sign-up checks it without collecting more than it needs.

features.name: Sign in with a passkey
features.does: Sign in with a passkey on a phone or computer, with no password to remember.

parts.name: Passkey sign-in
parts.what: Passkey registration and sign-in on the WebAuthn standard, using an open library whose licence suits the core.

parts.name: Password fallback
parts.what: An optional password, stored with a slow memory-hard hash and checked against known breached passwords.

parts.name: One-time code sign-in
parts.what: Signs in with a code sent by email or text where no passkey is set up.

parts.name: Sign-in screens
parts.what: Shared sign-in, account chooser and consent screens used by every app.

parts.name: Sign-in attack protection
parts.what: Slows repeated failed sign-ins, checks for credential stuffing across accounts, and locks out attackers without locking out the owner.

features.name: Keep my account secure
features.does: Turn on a second sign-in step, see every signed-in device and sign any of them out.

parts.name: Second sign-in step
parts.what: Authenticator codes or a second passkey, required for workers, moderators and admins.

parts.name: Sessions and devices
parts.what: Session tokens with expiry and refresh, a device list and remote sign-out.

parts.name: New sign-in alerts
parts.what: Tells the person when a new device or place signs in to their account.

parts.name: Fresh sign-in for risky commands
parts.what: Asks for a fresh sign-in with the second step before risky commands, such as changing payout or contact details, declared once in each command's schema and applied to people and agents alike.

features.name: Get back into a lost account
features.does: Recover an account after losing a phone or passkey, mostly without needing staff.

parts.name: Recovery codes and backup methods
parts.what: Recovery codes, a second email or phone, and a second passkey.

parts.name: Assisted recovery
parts.what: A support-run recovery path with an identity re-check and a waiting period, every step logged.

features.name: Have one profile and a role in each app
features.does: Keep one name and photo while being a rider in one app and a driver in another.

parts.name: Profile model
parts.what: Display name, photo, languages, pronouns and what each app may show.

parts.name: Roles per app
parts.what: Grants roles such as customer, worker, host or moderator per app, each with its own checks.

parts.name: Profile and roles page
parts.what: Edit the profile and see which roles are active in which app.

parts.name: Access needs
parts.what: Access needs saved on the profile with consent, such as a wheelchair, an assistance dog or 'message, don't call', and carried on every request and order.

parts.name: Profile photo checks
parts.what: Checks that a profile photo shows a face and nothing offensive before others see it, with any face check run under the Biometric Processing Privacy Code and never used to identify anyone. Spare Ride and Spare Stay need the same check.

features.name: Sign in to other apps with Spareware
features.does: Use a Spareware login in add-ins, member-run apps and AI agents, choosing what each may see.

parts.name: Sign-in provider
parts.what: An OpenID Connect and OAuth 2 provider with consent screens, scopes and token revocation.

parts.name: Connected apps page
parts.what: Lists every app and agent with access and removes any of them in one step.

features.name: Run a business or team account
features.does: Set up a restaurant, trade firm or office team with staff who act for it.

parts.name: Organisation model
parts.what: Organisations with members, roles, invites and owners, shared by every app.

parts.name: Team management
parts.what: Invite staff, set what each can do and remove them.

parts.name: Directory sync for offices and schools
parts.what: Brings people in from an organisation's own directory using open standards such as SCIM and LDAP.

parts.name: Organisation sign-in
parts.what: Lets staff sign in through their organisation's own identity provider using SAML or OpenID Connect, beside directory sync.

parts.name: Organisation policies
parts.what: Settings an organisation's admin can lock, such as AI tools off, no sharing outside the organisation and the region its data is kept in.

parts.name: Shared devices and staff PINs
parts.what: Quick staff switching with a PIN on a shared tablet or till, with each person's actions recorded under their own name and limited by their role.

parts.name: Organisation audit log
parts.what: Lets an organisation's admins see who did what across every app the organisation uses, built from the operation log, searchable and exportable, with its own retention. Spare Office, Spare Studio and Spare Construct need the same log.

parts.name: Organisation branding
parts.what: An organisation's logo, colours and fonts, set once and shown on its sign-in page, mail, forms and shared work, and locked as a brand kit where the admin chooses. Spare Office and Spare Studio need the same settings.

features.name: Let someone act for me
features.does: Let a carer, parent or assistant act for me within limits we can both see.

parts.name: Delegated access
parts.what: Time-limited, scoped permission for one account to act for another, shown in both accounts and logged.

parts.name: Rules for parents and carers
parts.what: What a parent or carer may see and do for a young person or someone they support, building on each app's minimum age.

features.name: Carry one identity across open networks
features.does: Use my Spareware identity as a handle on open social networks and move it to another host.

parts.name: Open network identity
parts.what: Links a Spareware account to a portable handle on the open protocols Spare Social chooses.

features.name: Sign in with another provider
features.does: Link a sign-in from another provider, where members have voted to allow it.

parts.name: Outside sign-in links
parts.what: Optional sign-in through other providers, off by default and subject to a member vote.

features.name: Change my email or phone
features.does: Change the email or phone on my account, with the new one checked and the old one told.

parts.name: Contact change
parts.what: Asks for a fresh sign-in, checks the new email or phone, tells the old one, and gives a short window to undo a change the owner did not make.

features.name: Sign in on a TV or command line
features.does: Sign in on a device with no keyboard or browser by entering a short code on my phone.

parts.name: Device sign-in
parts.what: Signs in TVs, command-line tools and other devices without a browser using a short code entered on another device, under OAuth device authorisation (RFC 8628).

features.name: Merge two accounts
features.does: Join two accounts I made by mistake, such as one by email and one by phone, into one.

parts.name: Account merge
parts.what: Merges two accounts that belong to one person after a fresh sign-in to both, keeping orders, ratings, roles and checks, and leaving one membership and one vote.

features.name: Switch between my accounts
features.does: Keep a personal and a work account signed in side by side, or several people's logins on a shared device, and switch in one step.

parts.name: Account switcher
parts.what: Keeps several accounts signed in on one device, each with its own sessions, and on a shared device locks each one behind its owner's own sign-in. Spare Office and Spare Social need the same switcher.

features.name: Try an app before signing up
features.does: Use a design app on my own computer with no account, and keep my settings and recent work if I sign up later.

parts.name: Local profile without an account
parts.what: Keeps preferences, recent files and libraries on the device with no account at all, and moves them into the account if the person later signs up. Spare Construct and Spare Studio both work this way.

features.name: Link family accounts
features.does: Link a parent's and a young person's accounts, with one payer and limits we can both see.

parts.name: Family accounts
parts.what: Links family accounts only when both agree, with a payer, settings for each age set by the rules, and a link the young person can always see. Spare Social, Spare Ride and Spare Food map the same need.

parts.name: Purchase approvals for children
parts.what: Holds a child's purchase, tip or booking until a parent approves it, with spending limits for each child, as app store laws ask. Spare Social and Spare OS need the same approvals.

features.name: Hand an organisation or project to a new owner
features.does: Hand an organisation, or a project with its history, to another member, who accepts before it changes.

parts.name: Ownership transfer
parts.what: Hands an organisation, or a project with its history, to another member, who accepts before anything changes, with both told and every step logged. Spare Office and Spare Construct need the same hand-over.

areas.name: Identity, licence and business checks
areas.summary: Proves people are who they say and hold the licences their work needs, through accredited providers and public registers. The co-op keeps the result; the provider keeps the documents under contract, and the co-op can get them back when the law asks. Built in svc-accounts; svc-identity is a proposed name (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Prove who I am
features.does: Confirm my identity once with a photo ID and a selfie, and reuse that result in every app that needs it.

parts.name: Identity provider choice
parts.what: Compares accredited identity providers in each country on cost, method and what data they keep, starting with those accredited under New Zealand's Digital Identity Services Trust Framework.

parts.name: Identity check link
parts.what: Sends a person to an accredited identity provider and receives only the result.

parts.name: Check results store
parts.what: Records what was checked, by whom, when and until when; the documents stay with the provider, and the co-op can retrieve them when the law asks.

parts.name: Biometric code compliance
parts.what: Meets the Biometric Processing Privacy Code 2025 for selfie and face-match checks: a proportionality assessment, clear notices, a non-biometric option and limits on keeping face data.

parts.name: Verification records on demand
parts.what: A contract under which the identity provider keeps verification records for the anti-money-laundering period, a way to retrieve them on request, and a legal hold that account deletion skips.

parts.name: Identity checks for people overseas
parts.what: Lets people who live outside the country an app runs in, such as overseas sellers and visiting guests, prove who they are in the first release, through a provider that covers their country or a local lawyer's anti-money-laundering identity check, recorded as the same result as a local check. Spare Home and Spare Stay both need it.

features.name: Show my work licence
features.does: Link a driver licence, trade registration or other licence so an app lets me take that work.

parts.name: Public register checks
parts.what: Looks up licences in public registers, such as trade boards and the business number register, on their published terms.

parts.name: Check rules per app
parts.what: Each app declares which checks a role needs and how often they repeat.

parts.name: My checks page
parts.what: Shows each check, its status and expiry, and what to do next.

features.name: Keep my checks current
features.does: Get reminded before a licence or check expires and renew it without starting over.

parts.name: Expiry and re-check scheduler
parts.what: Schedules re-checks and reminders, and pauses a role when a check lapses.

features.name: Ask for a failed check to be reviewed
features.does: Ask a person to review a check that failed or looks wrong.

parts.name: Check review request
parts.what: Lets a person explain and add evidence, and sends the request to the one review queue for a person to decide.

features.name: See what was verified about someone
features.does: See what was checked about a worker or host, and when, before working with them.

parts.name: Verified badge
parts.what: Shows which checks passed and their dates, without the details behind them.

features.name: Add a vehicle
features.does: Add a vehicle and have its registration and safety certificate checked.

parts.name: Vehicle data access
parts.what: Which official vehicle data an app may look up, on what terms and at what cost.

parts.name: Vehicle checks
parts.what: Checks registration and safety certificate status from sources that allow it.

features.name: Prove my business is real
features.does: Verify a business so it can sell, hire or host in any app.

parts.name: Business number lookup
parts.what: Confirms a business through each country's business register (example: the New Zealand Business Number register) and stores the result.

parts.name: Trader details
parts.what: Keeps the trader details marketplace law asks for and shows buyers what they are owed.

parts.name: Charities register check
parts.what: Confirms a registered charity through each country's charities register (example: New Zealand's Charities Register), on its published terms, and stores the result beside the business number check.

features.name: Prove my age without sharing more
features.does: Show an app I am old enough without handing over my birth date or a document.

parts.name: Age checks
parts.what: Age assurance through an accredited provider, returning only whether a person is over the age set.

features.name: Pass a safety check where the law needs one
features.does: Consent to a background check where an app's law requires it, and see the outcome.

parts.name: Background checks in each country
parts.what: Which checks each app's law requires, who may run them and how to do it lawfully.

parts.name: Background check link
parts.what: Requests a consented check from an approved provider and records only the outcome.

features.name: Use my checks in another country
features.does: Have identity and licence checks work with each country's own providers and registers.

parts.name: Check providers per country
parts.what: Identity, licence and register sources for each country added, in its country pack.

features.name: Show I may work here
features.does: Show that my visa lets me do this kind of work, as an employee or a contractor, before I take jobs.

parts.name: Right-to-work rules
parts.what: Which visas allow employment, which allow contracting, and what each app must check for its workers' status.

parts.name: Visa entitlement check
parts.what: Checks a worker's entitlement through an official visa check or the identity provider, records the result and its expiry, and re-checks before it lapses.

features.name: Prove it is still me
features.does: Pass a quick face re-check now and then, so no one else can work under my account.

parts.name: Face check fairness testing
parts.what: Tests re-check providers for error rates across skin tones, ages and genders, and publishes the results before any is used.

parts.name: Repeat face checks
parts.what: Random re-checks at the start of work to stop account renting, with a non-biometric option and a person reviewing every failure before any pause.

features.name: Have a document checked by a person
features.does: Upload a paper that has no public register, such as an insurance certificate or a warrant of fitness, and have a trained person check it.

parts.name: Document checks by a person
parts.what: Checks papers with no public register, such as insurance certificates, warrants and certificates of fitness and food registrations, by a trained person on the one review queue, recording each result with an expiry for the re-check scheduler.

features.name: Prove my address
features.does: Prove I live at or control an address, sharing only the result.

parts.name: Address check by posted code
parts.what: Confirms an address by a code sent by post, or by a trusted record such as a rates notice, and stores only the result and its date. Spare Market and Spare Home need it, and hosts and landlords can use the same check.

areas.name: Payments and payouts
areas.summary: Customers pay, a regulated provider holds the money within its time limits, workers are paid everything except the at-cost fee, and every dollar is shown, including who carries a loss, payments taken in person and payments made outside the app. The co-op never holds money or card numbers itself. Built as svc-payments.

features.name: Pay for a job
features.does: Pay by card or phone wallet in any app, seeing the full price before paying.

parts.name: Payment provider choice
parts.what: Compares providers that pay out to workers in each country, starting with New Zealand, and lists what Spareware must never handle itself.

parts.name: Payment provider link
parts.what: One adapter to the chosen regulated provider for charges, holds, splits, refunds and payouts.

parts.name: Checkout
parts.what: A shared checkout using the provider's own secure card fields, so card numbers never reach our servers.

parts.name: Money type
parts.what: Exact amounts in each currency's ISO 4217 minor units, with currency, rounding rules and sales tax fields: the one money type every app and kit-core use.

parts.name: Seller of record per app
parts.what: Decides for each app whether the worker or the co-op is the seller, which sets who charges sales tax, who owes consumer guarantees, whose name is on the receipt and who answers card disputes.

parts.name: Yearly card security check
parts.what: A yearly PCI DSS self-assessment, SAQ A while card fields stay with the provider, as the card schemes ask of every merchant and platform.

parts.name: Checkout without an account
parts.what: Whether people may order with no account, weighing card fraud, anti-money-laundering duties and data rights, decided once. Spare Food and Spare Market both wait on it.

features.name: Know my money is held until the job is done
features.does: Have my payment held by the provider, within its time limits, and released only when the job is confirmed.

parts.name: Hold and release rules
parts.what: Holds a payment against an order and releases, refunds or splits it when the order says so.

parts.name: Holding money lawfully
parts.what: A lawyer confirms how held money must be run so the co-op never holds it itself.

parts.name: Stage payments
parts.what: Holds and releases money in stages for longer jobs.

parts.name: Hold time limits
parts.what: Each provider's limits on holding money, with rules for when to charge bookings made far ahead, deposit then balance, and re-authorising card holds that expire.

features.name: Get paid out
features.does: Set up payouts once and receive everything I earned, less only the at-cost fee.

parts.name: Payout set-up
parts.what: Sends workers to the provider's own identity and bank account set-up, passing on the kit's identity check result where the provider accepts it, so a worker proves who they are once.

parts.name: Payout runs
parts.what: Pays out daily in batches, with faster payouts at the provider's cost where offered.

parts.name: Earnings page
parts.what: Shows each job, the fee, sales tax and every payout, and exports them.

parts.name: Payout change guard
parts.what: When a bank account, email or phone changes, asks for a fresh sign-in, holds payouts for a short time and alerts both the old and new contacts.

parts.name: Failed payouts
parts.what: Handles payouts a bank returns, such as for a closed account or wrong details, keeping the money with the provider, telling the worker and paying again once the details are fixed.

parts.name: Money that cannot be paid out
parts.what: What happens to money that can never be paid out, and how unclaimed money law applies to it (example: New Zealand's Unclaimed Money Act 1971; *unverified* period for platform balances).

parts.name: Bank account name check
parts.what: Checks the account name matches when payout details change, through the banks' own name check where a country has one (example: New Zealand banks' Confirmation of Payee, run since late 2024; *unverified* whether a business can call it), or the provider's own check.

features.name: See the at-cost fee
features.does: See exactly what the fee is, what it pays for and how it was worked out.

parts.name: Fee calculator
parts.what: Works out each job's fee from the period's published rate and passes provider charges through at cost.

parts.name: Fee breakdown
parts.what: Shows this job's fee and where every dollar goes on the price, the receipt and the earnings page, linking to how the period's fee was set.

parts.name: Card fee pass-through check
parts.what: Checks that passing card costs through at cost is not a card surcharge where the law bans one, such as in-store payments if New Zealand's planned ban applies (*unverified*).

features.name: Get a refund
features.does: Get a full or part refund when a job is cancelled or a dispute says so.

parts.name: Refunds
parts.what: Full and part refunds through the provider, following the order's cancellation policy.

parts.name: Card disputes
parts.what: Answers card disputes raised with banks, sending the order's evidence to the provider.

features.name: Tip the worker
features.does: Add a tip that goes to the worker in full.

parts.name: Tips
parts.what: Adds a tip during or after the job and pays all of it to the worker; the card cost on a tip is carried as a running cost in the at-cost fee, never taken from the tip.

features.name: Keep a receipt
features.does: Get a clear receipt showing the fee and sales tax for every payment.

parts.name: Receipts
parts.what: Issues receipts in the person's language, with a printable copy.

features.name: Save a card for next time
features.does: Save a card with the provider so paying next time is one tap.

parts.name: Saved payment methods
parts.what: Stores only the provider's token, never the card, and lets the person remove it.

features.name: Trust that every dollar adds up
features.does: Know that what the provider moved matches what every order says.

parts.name: Reconciliation
parts.what: Matches provider reports against orders and payouts daily and flags any gap.

features.name: Pay a deposit or damage hold
features.does: Pay a refundable deposit or damage hold for a stay or a hire.

parts.name: Deposits and damage holds
parts.what: Holds an amount and releases it by a set time unless a claim is made.

features.name: Pay straight from my bank
features.does: Pay from a bank account where the provider supports it.

parts.name: Bank payments
parts.what: Adds account-to-account payments through the provider as open banking reaches more banks.

features.name: Pay a regular amount
features.does: Pay monthly for shop hosting, storage or supporting a creator.

parts.name: Regular payments
parts.what: Monthly charges at cost with clear notice, pausing and one-step cancelling.

parts.name: Monthly caps and billing after use
parts.what: Lets a person set a monthly cap, warns before it is reached and charges for the month's use afterwards through the provider, so the co-op never holds a prepaid balance.

features.name: Be protected from payment fraud
features.does: Have stolen cards and fake accounts stopped before money moves.

parts.name: Provider fraud screening
parts.what: Uses the provider's own fraud screening and records its decision on the order.

parts.name: Published risk rules
parts.what: Published rules for new accounts, large amounts and fast repeat payments, starting from the provider's screening; the shared fraud signals service builds on them.

features.name: Pay and be paid in my own currency
features.does: Pay and be paid in the money of each country Spareware runs in.

parts.name: Currencies per country
parts.what: Prices, payouts and fees in each country's currency, with exchange costs published.

features.name: Give a gift card
features.does: Give someone a gift card for any Spareware app.

parts.name: Gift card rules
parts.what: What consumer and anti-money-laundering law say about gift cards and stored credit.

parts.name: Gift cards
parts.what: Gift cards held and settled by the provider, never by the co-op.

features.name: Know who carries a loss
features.does: Know what happens when a refund or a lost card dispute lands after the worker was already paid.

parts.name: Loss rules
parts.what: Who carries a late refund or a lost card dispute: recovery from future earnings, a protection pool or the co-op, and the platform's liability under the provider's terms.

parts.name: Negative balances
parts.what: Tracks what a worker owes after a late refund or lost dispute and recovers it from future payouts within published limits, never by surprise.

features.name: Pay on account as a business
features.does: Let a business pay on account and get one tax invoice a month.

parts.name: Business accounts on credit
parts.what: Lets an organisation book on account with spending limits for its staff, then charges it once a month with one tax invoice.

parts.name: Company travel and spending rules
parts.what: Simple company rules, such as a nightly price limit, where and when staff may travel and an amount per trip, checked at booking. Spare Ride and Spare Stay need the same rules.

features.name: Record a payment made outside the app
features.does: Record a job paid in cash or by bank transfer, so the order, ratings and records still work.

parts.name: Outside payment records
parts.what: Records a cash or bank transfer payment that both sides confirm, so the order, ratings, stock and records work as if it was paid in the app.

parts.name: Fee on outside payments
parts.what: Invoices the worker for the at-cost fee on a job paid outside the provider, under the fee rule each app's members chose.

parts.name: Cash checks
parts.what: Flags cash payments for the anti-money-laundering programme, such as large or repeated cash amounts, and counts them toward the due diligence threshold.

features.name: Take a card in person
features.does: Take a card payment at the end of a job on my own phone, a card reader or a shop till.

parts.name: Tap to pay on a phone
parts.what: Takes a card on the worker's own phone through the provider's tap to pay, which Stripe lists country by country (example: New Zealand; *unverified* for Connect platforms), with the in-store surcharge check applied.

parts.name: Card readers and a shared till
parts.what: The provider's card readers and a shared till for shops and restaurants, with quick staff switching on the shared device.

features.name: Keep taking payments if a provider drops us
features.does: Keep paying and being paid if the payment provider closes the co-op's account.

parts.name: Second provider and exit plan
parts.what: A second regulated provider ready behind the same adapter, and a tested plan to move to it, including moving saved card tokens through the providers' own migration process.

features.name: Split a payment with others
features.does: Split one payment between several people, each paying their share by a deadline.

parts.name: Split payments
parts.what: Splits one payment between several payers, each paying their share through the provider, with a deadline, reminders and a published rule for shares not paid in time.

features.name: Know what happens when a payment fails
features.does: Be told when a payment fails, fix it simply, and never be charged extra for the failure.

parts.name: Failed payment handling
parts.what: Retries a failed charge on a published schedule, tells the person, asks for another method and holds new bookings until any balance is paid, never adding a charge for the failure. Spare Ride, Spare Food, Spare Stay and Spare Rent need the same rules.

features.name: Raise money for a cause
features.does: Run a fundraiser or a fundraising sale for a school, club or charity.

parts.name: Fundraising rules
parts.what: Each country's rules for charitable fundraising, receipts and donation tax relief, starting with New Zealand's donation tax credits, for fundraisers in Spare Social and fundraising sales in Spare Market.

areas.name: Tax, invoices and money law
areas.summary: The tax and money law every marketplace must meet, built once and filled in by each country pack: sales tax on platform sales (example: New Zealand GST on listed services), the co-op's own sales tax returns, tax invoices, reporting sellers' income to the tax office (example: New Zealand's IRD), anti-money-laundering duties and record keeping. New Zealand is the first country pack; each country gets its own. Built in svc-payments; svc-tax is a proposed name (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Have sales tax charged correctly
features.does: Have sales tax worked out and collected the way each country's law says for each kind of job.

parts.name: Sales tax rules per app
parts.what: Maps which apps fall under each country's sales tax rules for platforms (example: New Zealand GST on listed services) and how each kind of job is taxed.

parts.name: Sales tax engine
parts.what: Works out sales tax on every order from the country pack's rules, including the platform's own duty to collect it where the law sets one (example: New Zealand GST on listed services).

parts.name: Flat-rate credit notices
parts.what: Tells unregistered sellers their flat-rate credits at least monthly, as the law asks.

features.name: Get a proper tax invoice
features.does: Get a valid tax invoice, or have the platform issue one for the seller where the law allows.

parts.name: Tax invoices
parts.what: Issues tax invoices and buyer-created tax invoices with every field the law asks for.

parts.name: Supply correction information
parts.what: Issues supply correction information, which replaced credit and debit notes from 1 April 2023, whenever a refund, an order change or an extra charge alters an amount already invoiced, with invoices numbered in order for each seller.

parts.name: Invoice numbers and payment terms
parts.what: Numbers each seller's invoices in order, with changes issued as supply correction information, and adds due dates, reminders and part payments for invoices paid later. Spare Work numbers invoices this way, and Spare Market's wholesale invoices need the terms.

features.name: Know my income is reported correctly
features.does: Have the platform report sellers' income to the tax office each year (example: New Zealand's IRD), and see what was sent.

parts.name: Platform reporting rules
parts.what: What the digital platform reporting rules ask for, which sellers are covered and when.

parts.name: Seller details
parts.what: Collects and checks the details reporting needs, including tax numbers.

parts.name: Yearly tax office report
parts.what: Builds and files the yearly report and gives each seller a copy.

features.name: Get a year-end statement
features.does: Download a year's earnings, fees and sales tax to give to an accountant.

parts.name: Yearly statements
parts.what: A yearly statement for each worker, printable and in open formats.

parts.name: Accounting exports
parts.what: Exports in open formats that common accounting software can import.

parts.name: Work mileage and expense log
parts.what: Work kilometres from finished jobs and time online, measured without keeping the route, and expenses with a receipt photo, gathered into a year-end tax pack.

features.name: Know the co-op meets anti-money-laundering law
features.does: Trust that the co-op follows anti-money-laundering law for online marketplaces.

parts.name: Anti-money-laundering programme
parts.what: A risk assessment, compliance programme and named compliance officer, checked by a lawyer.

parts.name: Customer checks
parts.what: Runs the checks the programme requires through the identity and payment providers, reusing the kit's identity check result and the provider's own checks wherever the law allows, so a person proves who they are once.

parts.name: Suspicious activity reports
parts.what: Flags, reviews and files reports to the authorities, with access kept to named people.

parts.name: Yearly compliance report
parts.what: Gathers the figures for the yearly report and the independent audit.

parts.name: Due diligence threshold
parts.what: Counts each person's transactions with the co-op over a rolling 12 months and starts customer due diligence once they pass the country pack's threshold (example: NZ$10,000 under the online marketplace exemption from New Zealand's DIA; *unverified* exact test), while suspicious activity reporting still covers everyone.

parts.name: Customer risk ratings
parts.what: Gives each person who passes the threshold a risk rating under the programme, keeps it on record and reviews it when their activity changes.

parts.name: Politically exposed people and enhanced checks
parts.what: Checks whether a person over the threshold is politically exposed, and runs enhanced due diligence where the risk rating or the law calls for it (*unverified* detail for marketplaces).

features.name: Know records are kept as long as the law says
features.does: Trust that every financial record is kept for the required time and can be produced.

parts.name: Financial record keeping
parts.what: Keeps orders, invoices and payouts for the required period in a tamper-evident log.

features.name: Have tax handled in other countries
features.does: Have each country's sales tax and platform reporting handled when an app goes overseas.

parts.name: Tax rules per country
parts.what: Country packs for each country's VAT, GST or other sales tax rules and platform reporting.

parts.name: Tax on services sold across borders
parts.what: Which sales taxes, VAT and digital services taxes apply when a member in another country pays for at-cost storage or AI, or a worker in another country sells remote services, and when the co-op must register there. Spare Studio and Spare Work both need the answer.

parts.name: Levies and tourist taxes
parts.what: Each place's levies, tourist taxes and per-trip charges as data in its country pack, such as a state's short-stay levy or a trip levy. Spare Stay and Spare Ride map the same need.

features.name: Know payouts never reach sanctioned people
features.does: Trust that payouts are screened against sanctions lists.

parts.name: Sanctions screening
parts.what: Uses the payment provider's screening and records the result.

features.name: Know the co-op pays its own sales tax
features.does: Trust that the co-op files its own sales tax returns as marketplace operator and charges sales tax on its fee.

parts.name: Co-op sales tax registration
parts.what: When the co-op must register for sales tax in each country, its return periods, and how platform rules make it the supplier of record (example: New Zealand's GST listed services rules).

parts.name: Operator sales tax returns
parts.what: Builds and files the co-op's sales tax returns as marketplace operator from the sales tax engine's records, ready for an accountant to check.

parts.name: Sales tax on the fee
parts.what: Charges sales tax on the at-cost fee where it applies and issues tax invoices for the fee to sellers registered for sales tax.

features.name: Opt out of platform sales tax as a large supplier
features.does: As a large accommodation owner or large registered supplier, agree with the platform to account for sales tax myself where the law allows.

parts.name: Sales tax opt-out agreements
parts.what: Records opt-out agreements where the law allows them (example: New Zealand's listed services rules), checks the size tests, and switches the sales tax engine to the seller accounting for the tax.

features.name: Get sales tax figures for each return
features.does: As a worker registered for sales tax, get the platform's figures for each return period (example: two-monthly or six-monthly in New Zealand).

parts.name: Sales tax period statements
parts.what: Statements for workers registered for sales tax that match their return periods, showing sales, the tax the platform collected and fees (*unverified* exact duty under New Zealand's listed services rules).

features.name: Have tax held back from my payouts
features.does: Choose a rate of tax to be held back from each payout and paid to the tax office for me.

parts.name: Voluntary withholding rules
parts.what: Confirms with the tax office how voluntary withholding works when a platform pays a contractor (example: New Zealand's IRD), and what each statement must show. Spare Food and Spare Work both map it.

parts.name: Withholding at payout
parts.what: Holds back the rate a worker chooses from each payout, passes it to the tax office and shows it on statements and the yearly summary.

features.name: Be warned before I must register for sales tax
features.does: Be told before my sales across every Spareware app reach the sales tax registration threshold.

parts.name: Sales tax threshold warning
parts.what: Warns a worker or seller whose sales across every Spareware app near the country's sales tax registration threshold (example: NZ$60,000 for New Zealand GST), and explains what registering changes. How platform sales count towards the threshold is for the sales tax study to confirm (*unverified*). Spare Food and Spare Market map the same warning.

areas.name: Marketplace engine
areas.summary: The one loop every marketplace runs (list or ask, match, agree, pay and hold, do the job, confirm, pay out, rate, resolve), plus changes, extra charges and promotions, built once in kit-market, with each app adding only its own rules.

features.name: List something
features.does: Create a listing for a ride, a meal, a stay, a home, a job or an item.

parts.name: Listing model
parts.what: One shared listing, with each app's own fields declared as a schema.

parts.name: Listing editor
parts.what: A shared editor for text, photos, prices and availability, plus each app's own fields.

parts.name: Listing checks
parts.what: Checks a listing against its app's published rules before it goes live.

parts.name: Accessibility features list
parts.what: One shared list of measurable access features, such as step-free entry and door width in centimetres, used on listings and in search filters, so Spare Stay, Spare Rent and Spare Home describe access the same way.

parts.name: Category trees
parts.what: Versioned category trees with translations, built from open classifications whose licence allows it and credited, which each app extends. Spare Work and Spare Market both need one.

features.name: Ask for something
features.does: Post a request, such as a ride or a job, and let workers respond.

parts.name: Request model
parts.what: A shared request with place, time, details and how it should be matched.

features.name: Agree a price
features.does: See the full price before agreeing, set by the app's own pricing rule.

parts.name: Pricing rules engine
parts.what: Metered, fixed, nightly, quoted, offer and auction prices as rules each app chooses.

parts.name: Full price first
parts.what: Works out every fee, tax and charge before any price is shown.

parts.name: Offers and quotes
parts.what: Offers, counter-offers and quotes, each with an expiry.

features.name: Follow an order from start to finish
features.does: See where an order is up to, from booking to paid out.

parts.name: Order steps
parts.what: The shared order steps as operations, with each app's own rules for moving between them.

parts.name: Order timeline
parts.what: Shows each step, who acted and what comes next, in every app.

parts.name: First marketplace
parts.what: Ranks Ride, Food, Work and others to choose which app proves the engine first.

features.name: Set when I am available
features.does: Set opening hours, free dates or shifts, and sync calendars from other booking sites.

parts.name: Availability calendars
parts.what: Time slots, blocked dates and capacity for each listing or worker.

parts.name: Calendar import and export
parts.what: iCalendar sync with other booking sites, catching double bookings.

parts.name: Repeat and time-zone engine
parts.what: Repeating events and their exceptions on the iCalendar standard, with current time-zone data including the Chatham Islands, used by every calendar, repeat booking and recurring job.

parts.name: Calendar screens
parts.what: Shared day, week, month and many-listing calendar views, with drag to move and tap to block, used by Spare Stay, Spare Work and Spare Office's bookings.

parts.name: Booking reminders and change links
parts.what: Confirmations and reminders before a booking or viewing, links to move or cancel it within the policy, and a message to everyone booked when it changes. Spare Home, Spare Rent, Spare Office, Spare Social and Spare Market need the same.

parts.name: Personal calendar feeds
parts.what: A private calendar feed of a person's own bookings, trips and viewings that any calendar app can subscribe to. Spare Stay, Spare Rent and Spare Social need it.

features.name: Cancel fairly
features.does: Cancel a booking knowing the cost in advance, under the policy in force when I booked.

parts.name: Cancellation and no-show policies
parts.what: Versioned policies stored with each booking and set by each app's members.

features.name: Confirm the job is done
features.does: Confirm a job is done, or have it confirm itself after a set time if nobody objects.

parts.name: Completion and auto-confirm
parts.what: Confirmation by both sides, with a timer that releases payment if nobody objects.

parts.name: Proof of handover
parts.what: Handover codes, photos and location stamps that show a job happened.

features.name: See my orders
features.does: Find past and current orders, receipts and messages, and book again.

parts.name: Orders page
parts.what: Lists orders with search, receipts and rebooking.

features.name: Book ahead or repeat a booking
features.does: Book for a later time, or set a booking to repeat weekly.

parts.name: Scheduled and repeat bookings
parts.what: Future and repeating orders that match and charge at the right time.

features.name: Keep stock right everywhere I sell
features.does: Keep stock counts right across an online shop, a market listing and a shop till.

parts.name: Stock
parts.what: Stock levels and reservations shared by every sales channel.

features.name: Run a job with several parties
features.does: Run an order that needs more than one party, such as a restaurant and a courier.

parts.name: Multi-party orders
parts.what: Orders split between parties, each with its own steps and payout.

features.name: Save favourites
features.does: Save favourite workers, listings and places to use again.

parts.name: Favourites
parts.what: Saved listings, workers and places for each person.

parts.name: Shortlists with notes and compare
parts.what: Adds private notes, sharing with chosen people and a side-by-side compare of facts and full prices to saved listings. Spare Home, Spare Rent and Spare Stay need the same.

features.name: Add a new marketplace without changing the engine
features.does: Let a new app add its own rules as plug-ins instead of changing the engine.

parts.name: App rule plug-ins
parts.what: Pricing, matching and step rules supplied by each app as sandboxed plugins.

features.name: Use a discount or voucher
features.does: Use a discount code, voucher or referral credit, and see who pays for it.

parts.name: Promotion rules
parts.what: What fair trading law asks of promotions, vouchers and referral credit, and who may fund them: the worker, a business or the co-op's budget.

parts.name: Promotions and vouchers
parts.what: Discount codes, vouchers and referral credit as pricing rules, each showing who pays for it, so no worker's pay is cut without their say.

features.name: Change an order or add a charge
features.does: Change a booking after it is made, or agree an extra charge after the job, with evidence and consent.

parts.name: Order changes
parts.what: A new time, an extra stop, more items or a longer stay, with the new price agreed by both sides and the held amount updated.

parts.name: Extra charges after the job
parts.what: Cleaning, tolls, damage or agreed variations added after the job, each with evidence, the customer's consent or a route to a dispute.

features.name: Choose the right kind of service
features.does: Pick a service type from one shared list, so every app knows what it includes and which checks the worker needs.

parts.name: Service catalogue
parts.what: One shared list of service types, what each includes, when it is usually needed and which checks a worker needs, used by listings and requests in Work, Home, Rent and Stay.

parts.name: Catalogue entries
parts.what: Each professional's or local service's offer listed once in the shared service catalogue, with its checks, prices and reviews, so Spare Home, Spare Rent and Spare Stay book the same pro that Spare Work lists, with one account and one payout.

features.name: Bring my listings from another platform
features.does: Bring my own listings, menus, product lists and calendars across from another platform without retyping them.

parts.name: Import terms
parts.what: What each source's terms let a member bring across, such as their own reviews, and what must stay behind.

parts.name: Bulk import
parts.what: Imports a member's own listings, menus, product lists and calendars from spreadsheets, exports and published feeds, checked against the app's rules before anything goes live.

features.name: Send a parcel or goods
features.does: Book a courier to carry a parcel or goods from one place to another.

parts.name: Delivery job type
parts.what: A shared A-to-B delivery job type for parcels and goods, with size limits, banned items and proof of delivery, that Food couriers carry and Market sellers can book.

features.name: Put things in a cart
features.does: Gather items from one or more sellers in a cart and check out once.

parts.name: Cart
parts.what: Items from one or many sellers with options and notes, kept on the device and the server, and split into one order per seller at checkout. Spare Food and Spare Market both need it.

features.name: Bring others into an order
features.does: Invite others onto a booking or a shared cart, or book for someone else.

parts.name: People on an order
parts.what: Invites co-travellers, flatmates or friends onto an order, or shares one cart that several people edit, each seeing only what they need. Spare Stay, Spare Food and Spare Ride map the same need.

parts.name: Book for someone else
parts.what: Books for a named person whose contact details are used only for that order, with a notice telling them what was shared. Spare Ride, Spare Stay and Spare Food all do this.

features.name: Pause or go away
features.does: Pause taking orders, set my hours, or mark my listings as away until I return.

parts.name: Away and pause
parts.what: Pauses orders for a set time, sets regular hours and holiday closures, or marks listings as away with a message and a return date. Spare Food and Spare Market both need it.

features.name: Get back something I left behind
features.does: Report an item I left in a car or a stay and get it back.

parts.name: Lost property
parts.what: Reports a lost item, opens a masked contact with the worker or host for a set time, tracks the return and pays any published return fee to the person who returns it. Spare Ride and Spare Stay need the same flow.

features.name: See how my listings are doing
features.does: See views, orders, sales and what needs doing across my listings, in totals that track nobody.

parts.name: Insights for sellers and hosts
parts.what: Counts of views, orders, sales, fees and refunds for each listing, worked out from the operation log in totals only, with simple charts and downloads. Spare Food, Spare Stay, Spare Market, Spare Home and Spare Social map the same need.

parts.name: Seller to-do page
parts.what: One page of what needs doing across listings, orders, offers, questions and disputes.

features.name: Know a fair price
features.does: See what similar things sold or let for, to set or judge a price.

parts.name: Sold price records
parts.what: Final prices of finished sales and lets, kept without the buyer's name and shown only where the law and the source's terms allow.

parts.name: Price guides
parts.what: A likely price range from similar recent sales or listings, with every step of the working visible, shown while pricing and searching. Spare Home, Spare Rent and Spare Market need the same guide.

features.name: Run an auction
features.does: Sell by auction, online or in a room, with every bidder seeing the same bids.

parts.name: Auction law
parts.what: What consumer law, auction rules and in-trade disclosure ask of online and in-room auctions, including who may run a home auction and the rules on seller bids and reserves.

parts.name: Live auction engine
parts.what: Bids as operations ordered by the server, one server clock, a public bid history, automatic bids and extensions near the end, so every bidder sees the same truth. Spare Home and Spare Market share it.

parts.name: Bidder registration
parts.what: Registers and checks bidders before an auction, with the checks the law or the seller asks for.

parts.name: Fake bid checks
parts.what: Flags bids from accounts linked to the seller or to each other, by device, payment or address signals, as rules on the shared fraud signals service.

features.name: Know what may be sold or offered
features.does: Know which goods and services are banned or need a licence, and why.

parts.name: Restricted goods and services law
parts.what: Every law in each country pack that limits what may be sold or offered online, starting with New Zealand's, such as alcohol, vapes, medicines, firearms and work reserved to licensed people, with sources. Spare Market, Spare Work and Spare Food all need it.

parts.name: Banned and restricted rules
parts.what: Banned, restricted and licence-needed items and services as versioned rules linked to categories and keywords, changed by member vote within the law and checked when a listing is made.

parts.name: Rules pages
parts.what: Plain pages listing what can and cannot be sold or offered, and why.

features.name: Change many listings at once
features.does: Change the price, stock or dates of many listings in one step, and undo it in one step.

parts.name: Bulk edit
parts.what: Changes price, stock, dates or settings for many listings in one checked operation that can be undone together. Spare Stay and Spare Market both need it.

features.name: See a listing's history
features.does: See a listing's price changes, relists and time on the market.

parts.name: Public listing history
parts.what: Shows price changes, relists, time on the market and changes made after someone engaged, drawn from the operation log with personal details removed. Spare Home and Spare Market both show it.

features.name: Answer questions about a listing
features.does: See every question about my listing in one place and answer it, privately or for everyone.

parts.name: Enquiry inbox
parts.what: One inbox for every question about a listing, linked to the asker's profile, with quick replies, files and answers the lister can publish for everyone. Spare Home and Spare Rent both need it.

features.name: Book a service from another app
features.does: Book a pro or add a ride, meal or cleaner from another Spareware app without leaving the one I am in.

parts.name: Bookings across apps
parts.what: Books a service from the shared catalogue, or adds another app's service to an order, such as an airport ride, a meal or a cleaner, as a linked kit-market order, so no app calls another app's code. Spare Home, Spare Stay and Spare Rent book Spare Work's pros this way.

parts.name: Which ledger carries a cross-app booking
parts.what: Records each cross-app booking against the app it was booked from, so its fee and cost show once, in one app's ledger.

features.name: See what I looked at recently
features.does: Go back to listings I looked at, kept private to me.

parts.name: Recently viewed
parts.what: A private list of listings a person looked at, kept on the device unless they choose to sync it. Spare Stay and Spare Market both offer it.

features.name: Order without the app
features.does: Book or order by text or phone when I cannot or would rather not use the app.

parts.name: Text ordering and booking
parts.what: Books or orders by text from a favourite or a past order, with updates by text, a PIN or an approval in the app for a saved card, and the text cost guard. Spare Ride books this way, and Spare Food maps the same channel.

parts.name: Phone ordering line
parts.what: A phone number with a simple menu and a person who takes the order into the same order path, including calls through a relay service (example: New Zealand Relay). Spare Ride and Spare Food both need it.

areas.name: Search, matching and dispatch
areas.summary: Pairs a request with the right worker or listing (search with filters, nearest driver, ready-timed courier, open dates, best quote) using rules anyone can read, fair to workers and customers alike. Built in svc-matching; svc-search is a proposed name (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Search listings
features.does: Search by words, place, date and price, with results ranked by published rules.

parts.name: Search engine choice
parts.what: Compares open search engines on speed, licence and running cost.

parts.name: Search service
parts.what: The one search service: full-text, filter and map search for listings and any other content an app declares, for every app.

parts.name: Published ranking rules
parts.what: Ranking rules anyone can read, with no paid placement.

parts.name: Audience filters
parts.what: Shows each search result only to the people its owner chose, so posts, files and groups can be searched as safely as listings.

parts.name: Search screens
parts.what: Shared search box, suggestions, recent searches, filter chips, sorting and result lists that work on a phone and with a screen reader, which each app fills with its own fields. Every marketplace, Spare Office and Spare Social build on them.

features.name: Go online for work
features.does: Go online or offline, and set where, when and how much work I take on.

parts.name: Worker availability
parts.what: Online status, work areas, capacity and breaks for each worker.

features.name: Get matched quickly
features.does: Have a request sent to the best worker nearby within seconds.

parts.name: Live location index
parts.what: A hexagon-grid index of where workers are, updated in real time.

parts.name: Dispatch engine
parts.what: Sends offers to workers in turn, with timeouts and passing on.

parts.name: Matching rules per app
parts.what: Each app's scoring rules, such as distance, ready time or trade, as plugins.

parts.name: Access-aware matching
parts.what: Matches a request only with workers and listings that meet the access needs it carries, and sends any refusal of an access need to a person for review.

features.name: Accept or decline work fairly
features.does: See the job and pay before accepting, and decline without hidden penalties.

parts.name: Job offer screen
parts.what: Shows the job, pay, distance and time before accepting.

parts.name: Fair offer rules
parts.what: Published, member-voted rules on declines, with no hidden throttling.

parts.name: Automated acceptance rules
parts.what: Published, member-voted rules for scripts and agents that accept offers or grab bookings, so bots do not beat people to work or scarce bookings.

parts.name: More time to answer offers
parts.what: Lets a worker choose a longer time to answer offers when they need it, as WCAG 2.2.1 asks of time limits, with dispatch allowing for it.

parts.name: Fair queues
parts.what: Per-person caps and a fair queue for scarce viewings, applications and limited releases, so nobody, person or script, takes every slot. Spare Rent and Spare Market need it.

features.name: Know why I was matched
features.does: See why a worker or listing was matched or ranked where it was.

parts.name: Match explanations
parts.what: A plain reason with each match and each ranking.

parts.name: Fairness checks
parts.what: Regular checks that offers, rankings and declines are fair to workers and to customers, with results published through the public reporting pipeline.

parts.name: Decline pattern checks
parts.what: Spots workers or hosts declining people in patterns that point to discrimination on grounds human rights law protects (example: New Zealand's Human Rights Act 1993), for a person to review.

parts.name: Measuring discrimination without collecting ethnicity
parts.what: Measures gaps in how groups of people are treated without storing members' ethnicity, porting a published privacy-preserving method such as Airbnb's Project Lighthouse, with a privacy impact assessment first.

features.name: Get quotes from several workers
features.does: Send one request to several suitable workers and compare their quotes.

parts.name: Quote requests
parts.what: Sends a request to a shortlist and gathers quotes side by side.

features.name: Take jobs going the same way
features.does: Let a worker take two jobs on the same route where the app allows it.

parts.name: Batching
parts.what: Groups compatible jobs by route and time.

features.name: Save a search
features.does: Save a search and be told when something new matches.

parts.name: Saved searches
parts.what: Stores searches and sends alerts through the person's chosen channels.

features.name: See where work is busy
features.does: See where and when demand is high, to choose where to work.

parts.name: Demand maps
parts.what: Demand by area and hour, shown only in groups large enough to protect privacy.

parts.name: Demand forecasts
parts.what: Short-term demand forecasts by area and hour from past orders, events and weather, using proven open methods, shown only in groups large enough to protect privacy. Spare Ride and Spare Food both map them.

features.name: Get suggestions I can switch off
features.does: See suggestions based on my past use, with reasons shown and an off switch.

parts.name: Explainable suggestions
parts.what: Simple suggestions that explain themselves and run only with consent.

areas.name: Maps, places and live location
areas.summary: Maps, address search, routing, live location and service areas on open data, so no app depends on a paid map provider, with exact places kept private until a booking needs them. Built as svc-maps.

features.name: See a map
features.does: See a fast map of where a job or listing is, in every app.

parts.name: Map tiles
parts.what: Vector tiles built from OpenStreetMap data and served at cost.

parts.name: Map display
parts.what: Map display with MapLibre, styled to the design guide.

parts.name: Map data licence
parts.what: Meets OpenStreetMap's licence: attribution shown and share-alike handled for any changed data.

parts.name: Maps in words
parts.what: A list view, written directions and areas described in words beside every map, so screen reader users get the same information.

features.name: Find an address
features.does: Type an address or place and pick it from suggestions.

parts.name: Geocoder choice
parts.what: Compares open geocoders on address quality in each country, starting with New Zealand, and on licence, keeping any GPL engine as a separate service.

parts.name: Address search
parts.what: Address and place search with suggestions as you type.

parts.name: Official address data
parts.what: Loads each country's official address data under its open licence, starting with New Zealand's, and keeps it current.

parts.name: Address from a pin
parts.what: Turns a pin or GPS position into the nearest address.

features.name: Get a route and arrival time
features.does: See the route and a reliable arrival time for a job.

parts.name: Routing engine choice
parts.what: Compares open routing engines on travel-time accuracy in each country, starting with New Zealand, and on speed, licence and running cost.

parts.name: Routing service
parts.what: Routes, travel times and distance tables for every app.

parts.name: Arrival time estimates
parts.what: Arrival times that learn from finished trips without keeping anyone's trace.

parts.name: Map matching
parts.what: Snaps GPS traces to roads to measure distance accurately for metered fares, pay by distance and the mileage log, using the open routing engine's map matching.

features.name: Share my location only during a job
features.does: Let the other side see where I am, only while the job is running.

parts.name: Live location stream
parts.what: Real-time positions that stop when the job ends and are not kept afterwards.

parts.name: Trip trace
parts.what: Keeps a job's route only where the law, safety or a dispute needs it.

parts.name: Faked location checks
parts.what: Spots simulated or spoofed positions from device signals and impossible movement, and flags them for review before fares or payouts rely on them.

features.name: Set the area I serve
features.does: Draw the area a worker or business serves, or where an app runs.

parts.name: Service areas
parts.what: Area shapes, checks for whether a place is inside, and app launch areas.

parts.name: Area editor
parts.what: Draws and changes service areas, zones and fare regions on a map, each change a versioned operation. Spare Ride and Spare Food both need it.

parts.name: Launch readiness
parts.what: Counts workers, customers and sellers signed up in each launch area against published targets before the area opens. Spare Food and Spare Ride plan launches this way.

features.name: Get turn-by-turn directions
features.does: Get spoken directions in the app, or hand off to my phone's map app.

parts.name: Turn-by-turn guidance
parts.what: Spoken guidance from the routing service, or a hand-off to the phone's own map app.

features.name: Use maps with no signal
features.does: Keep a map and my job addresses working without a connection.

parts.name: Offline map packs
parts.what: Downloadable map areas for workers in places with weak signal.

features.name: Fix a map mistake
features.does: Report a wrong address or road so it gets fixed for everyone.

parts.name: Map fix reports
parts.what: Sends fixes to OpenStreetMap, where the open data is kept.

features.name: See the right local time and places
features.does: See local time zones and points of interest correctly in every country.

parts.name: Time zones and places
parts.what: Time zone lookup by place, and open points of interest.

features.name: Keep my exact place private until booked
features.does: Show an approximate area on listings and profiles, and the exact address only once a booking is confirmed.

parts.name: Approximate location
parts.what: Blurs a place to an area on maps and in search, and reveals the exact address to the other side only when the order reaches the step that needs it.

features.name: See the facts about a place
features.does: See the hazards, zones and local rules that apply to an address, with their sources.

parts.name: Area data sources
parts.what: Which open sources exist for natural hazards, such as flood, liquefaction and coastal hazards, and for zoning, school zones and transport, under what licence and at what cost. Spare Construct, Spare Home and Spare Rent need the same answer.

parts.name: Area layers and lookups
parts.what: Hazard, zone and school zone layers on the map, and a lookup for any address, from sources whose licence allows it, each shown with its source and date.

parts.name: Council rules as data
parts.what: Each council's rules that apps apply, such as short-stay registration and night caps, sign rules and planning rules, kept as dated data with sources. Spare Stay, Spare Home and Spare Construct need them.

features.name: See boundaries on aerial photos
features.does: See a section's boundaries drawn on an aerial photo.

parts.name: Aerial photos and boundary lines
parts.what: Adds open aerial imagery and property boundary lines from each country's land agency (example: LINZ in New Zealand) to the kit's maps under their licences. Spare Home and Spare Construct both need them.

features.name: Count public transport in travel times
features.does: See travel times by bus and train as well as by car.

parts.name: Public transport timetables
parts.what: Imports the open timetable feeds (GTFS) that transport agencies publish, under their terms, so travel times can include buses and trains. Spare Ride and Spare Rent both need them.

areas.name: Messaging and notifications
areas.summary: Chat between the two sides of a job, calls that hide phone numbers, video calls, push, email, text and letters by post, with each member choosing what reaches them. Built in svc-messaging; svc-calls is a proposed name (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Chat about a job
features.does: Message the other side of a job, with photos, until the job is closed.

parts.name: Chat protocol choice
parts.what: Compares Matrix with building chat on the kit, including licences: Matrix's main servers, Synapse and Dendrite, are AGPL, so one could only ever run as a separate service, never in the core.

parts.name: Chat service
parts.what: The one chat server for every app, Spare Office's chat included: job chats and group chats, stored as operations and synced to every device.

parts.name: Chat screens
parts.what: Shared chat screens with photos, read receipts and quick replies.

parts.name: Link previews without tracking
parts.what: Our server fetches a link's title and picture once and shows them to readers, so the linked site never sees who read it, and never inside end-to-end encrypted chats.

parts.name: Interception duty check
parts.what: Whether the co-op's chat and call services make it a service provider with a duty to assist under interception law (example: New Zealand's Telecommunications (Interception Capability and Security) Act 2013; *unverified* whether app chat counts).

parts.name: Bridges to other chat networks
parts.what: Whether links to other chat networks are allowed by their terms, and how to join only those without weakening encryption. Spare Office and Spare Social share this question.

features.name: Call without sharing my number
features.does: Phone the other side of a job without either of us seeing the other's number.

parts.name: Masked calls
parts.what: Temporary numbers from a phone provider, paid at cost, that stop working after the job.

features.name: Get push notifications
features.does: Get alerts on my phone or computer for the things I care about.

parts.name: Push delivery
parts.what: Sends push through Apple's and Google's push services and web push, as phones require.

parts.name: Notification router
parts.what: Chooses the channel for each alert from the person's settings, with retries.

parts.name: Notification inbox
parts.what: One place in each app to see every alert.

parts.name: Private push content
parts.what: Push sent through Apple and Google carries only a wake-up signal or encrypted content, never message text in the clear.

features.name: Get emails and texts
features.does: Get receipts, codes and urgent alerts by email or text.

parts.name: Email sending
parts.what: Sends email through a provider paid at cost, handling bounces and complaints.

parts.name: Text sending
parts.what: Sends texts through a provider paid at cost, for codes and urgent alerts.

parts.name: Message templates
parts.what: Templates for each app and language, with plain-text copies.

parts.name: Text cost guard
parts.what: Limits on texted codes by number, country and hour, with alerts on unusual volume, to stop SMS pumping fraud running up an at-cost bill.

parts.name: Sender authentication
parts.what: SPF, DKIM and DMARC on every sending domain, and a page where a member can check that an email really came from Spareware.

features.name: Choose what reaches me
features.does: Turn each kind of alert on or off for each channel, and set quiet hours.

parts.name: Notification settings
parts.what: Choices by type and channel, plus quiet hours, shared by every app.

parts.name: Consent for messages
parts.what: Meets spam law: consent, a named sender and one-step unsubscribe for anything not essential.

parts.name: Digests
parts.what: Daily or weekly summaries by email or in the app instead of single alerts, chosen for each kind of alert. Spare Social, Spare Office, Spare Work, Spare Market and Spare Home all offer them.

features.name: Block and report from a chat
features.does: Block someone or report a message straight from the chat.

parts.name: Report from chat
parts.what: Report and block actions on every message, attaching the message to the report.

features.name: Read messages in my language
features.does: Read messages from the other side translated into my language.

parts.name: Message translation
parts.what: Optional translation of chat messages, with the original one tap away.

features.name: Hear from the co-op
features.does: Get co-op news, votes and meeting notices in one place.

parts.name: Co-op announcements
parts.what: Messages from the co-op and each app to members who chose to receive them.

features.name: Be warned about scams in chat
features.does: See a warning when a message looks like a scam or asks me to pay outside the app.

parts.name: Scam warnings
parts.what: Scam warnings in chat, as rules on the shared fraud signals service, with no message content sent elsewhere.

features.name: Keep private chats unreadable to anyone else
features.does: Have private chats that even the co-op cannot read.

parts.name: End-to-end encryption choice
parts.what: When chats should be end-to-end encrypted, and how that fits with reports and disputes.

features.name: Make a video call
features.does: Make a video call with one person or a group, in any app, at cost.

parts.name: Call method choice
parts.what: Compares open WebRTC servers and relay servers on licence, quality and running cost, together with Spare Office.

parts.name: Call service
parts.what: One-to-one and group video calls over WebRTC for every app, with relay servers run at cost.

features.name: Discuss in threads
features.does: Discuss a proposal, a cost line, a suggestion or a file in a thread, with replies and mentions.

parts.name: Threads and comments
parts.what: One threaded discussion part, with replies, mentions, reports and moderation, used by proposals, the member forum, suggestions, ledger questions, panel discussion, consultations and comments on files.

parts.name: Anchored comments
parts.what: Comments pinned to a point, region, page, video frame or text range, with replies and mentions, that map to and from PDF annotations. Spare Studio, Spare Office and Spare Construct's markups need the same model.

features.name: Reuse my replies
features.does: Save replies I send often and answer in one tap.

parts.name: Saved replies
parts.what: Reusable replies with fields such as a name and dates, and answers a lister can publish for everyone. Spare Stay, Spare Rent and Spare Work need them.

features.name: Schedule a message
features.does: Write a message now and have it sent at a set time or when something happens.

parts.name: Scheduled and automatic messages
parts.what: Messages sent at a chosen time or on a trigger, such as the day before arrival, each labelled as automatic. Spare Stay, Spare Social and Spare Office need them.

features.name: Run a quick poll
features.does: Ask a quick question in a chat, post or meeting and see the answers live.

parts.name: Quick polls
parts.what: One-question polls in a chat, a post, a meeting or a live talk, one vote per person and never by an agent, with live results, kept apart from binding member votes. Spare Social and Spare Office both need them.

features.name: Keep encrypted chats safe on every device
features.does: Have private group chats stay unreadable to anyone else on every device I use, with a backup only I can open.

parts.name: Encryption library
parts.what: One library for end-to-end encrypted group chats on the MLS standard, with each device holding its own keys, members joining and leaving safely, and backups the co-op cannot read, using openly licensed code. Spare Social and Spare Office both need it.

features.name: Get a letter by post
features.does: Get a code or a formal notice by post when the law or a check needs one.

parts.name: Posted letters
parts.what: Prints and posts letters, notices and codes through a mail provider paid at cost, recording the posting date as evidence. Spare Home's owner notices, Spare Rent's posted notices and Spare Market's address checks all need it.

features.name: See captions in a call
features.does: Read live captions in a call or meeting, in my language if I ask.

parts.name: Live captions in calls
parts.what: Live captions in voice and video calls and meetings, with speaker names, made on each person's device in encrypted calls and translated if a viewer asks. Spare Social and Spare Office both need them.

areas.name: Ratings and reputation
areas.summary: Two-way ratings and reviews after real jobs, made by people and never agents, fair rules on what counts, and a reputation members can see, challenge and take with them. Built as svc-trust.

features.name: Rate after a job
features.does: Rate the other side after a job, and see their rating of me only once we have both rated.

parts.name: Ratings service
parts.what: Two-way ratings tied to finished orders and revealed together.

parts.name: Rating screen
parts.what: A quick star rating with optional tags and a comment.

features.name: Write and answer reviews
features.does: Write a public review, and reply once to a review about me.

parts.name: Reviews
parts.what: Written reviews with one reply each, always linked to a real job.

parts.name: Fair review rules
parts.what: What may be published about people, and how defamation complaints are handled.

features.name: Not be marked down for what I can't control
features.does: Have ratings that blame things outside my control set aside.

parts.name: Rating exclusions
parts.what: Rules that set aside ratings caused by things like a slow kitchen or traffic.

features.name: Know the rating rules
features.does: See the rating levels that lead to a warning or a pause, set by member vote.

parts.name: Rating thresholds
parts.what: Published, voted thresholds with a warning and time to improve before any pause.

parts.name: Rating bias checks
parts.what: Checks ratings for bias against groups of workers, using the privacy-safe measurement method, before any rating can lead to a warning or a pause.

features.name: Challenge a rating or review
features.does: Ask for a rating or review to be checked and removed if it breaks the rules.

parts.name: Rating challenge
parts.what: Sends a challenge with the order's facts to the one review queue, where member moderators decide.

features.name: Show my reputation
features.does: Show jobs done, ratings and checks passed on my profile.

parts.name: Reputation summary
parts.what: A profile summary of jobs done, ratings and checks passed.

features.name: Take my reputation with me
features.does: Export my ratings and reviews in an open, signed format others can check.

parts.name: Portable reputation
parts.what: Signed exports of ratings and reviews that anyone can verify.

features.name: Trust that reviews are real
features.does: Know reviews come from real jobs and fake ones are removed.

parts.name: Fake review checks
parts.what: Flags review rings and paid reviews from order and account patterns, as rules on the shared fraud signals service.

features.name: Earn badges by published rules
features.does: Earn badges for good service under rules members set, and know how a badge is lost.

parts.name: Earned badges
parts.what: Badges earned from published criteria, such as reply time or cancellations, with criteria set by member vote and each badge saying how it is lost. Spare Rent, Spare Stay, Spare Market and Spare Social map the same need.

areas.name: Safety, reports and moderation
areas.summary: Keeps people safe during a job and online: emergency help that works anywhere, official alerts and a disaster mode, helplines, a safe path for sexual harm reports, reports, blocking, published rules, fair treatment whoever you are, member moderators, legal notices, known-illegal-content checks and a public log of every removal. Built as svc-trust.

features.name: Get help in an emergency
features.does: Call emergency services from inside a job, with my location and the job details ready to read out.

parts.name: Emergency button
parts.what: Calls the emergency number from the country pack (111 in New Zealand) and shows the address, vehicle and job details to read out, and still works with no data connection.

parts.name: Urgent safety lane
parts.what: The safety lane of the one urgent route, so urgent safety reports reach a trained person on the shared on-call roster at any hour.

parts.name: Helplines and emergency text
parts.what: Shows each country's helplines, such as 1737 in New Zealand, and guides Deaf and speech-impaired members to register for emergency text, such as 111 TXT in New Zealand, before they need it.

features.name: Share my trip with someone I trust
features.does: Send a friend a live link to my trip or job.

parts.name: Trusted contact link
parts.what: A time-limited link showing live progress, which ends with the job.

features.name: Report a problem
features.does: Report a person, listing, message or post, and follow what happens to my report.

parts.name: Reports service
