parts.what: Reports with categories, attachments and status, all as operations.

parts.name: Report forms
parts.what: Short report forms in every app, reachable from anything that can be reported.

parts.name: Reports without an account
parts.what: A public form anyone can use without an account, such as neighbours, people shown in a listing and rights holders, with abuse limits on the shared limiter.

features.name: Block someone
features.does: Block a person so they can't contact me or be matched with me again.

parts.name: Blocking
parts.what: Blocks that apply across chat, matching and feeds in every app.

features.name: Read the rules
features.does: Read each app's rules in plain words, with every past version.

parts.name: Rules library
parts.what: Versioned rules for each app and the whole co-op, changed only by member vote.

features.name: Have reports handled by trained members
features.does: Have reports reviewed by trained, elected members following clear steps.

parts.name: Moderation design
parts.what: Published rules, member-elected moderators, appeals, the public removal log and personal filters.

parts.name: Review queue
parts.what: The one queue for reports, check reviews, rating challenges and appeals, with assignment, decisions and reasons, all as operations.

parts.name: Moderator tools
parts.what: Review screens with context, history, blurring for distressing content and decision templates.

parts.name: Moderator wellbeing
parts.what: Exposure limits, breaks and support for people reviewing hard content.

features.name: See every removal in public
features.does: See a public log of every removal or ban and the rule behind it.

parts.name: Public removal log
parts.what: Publishes each decision with its rule and no personal details, through the public reporting pipeline.

features.name: Know why action was taken against me
features.does: Get a clear statement of what was done, which rule applied and how to appeal.

parts.name: Statements of reasons
parts.what: Sends the person affected the reason and an appeal link with every decision.

features.name: Have legal complaints handled on time
features.does: Have legal complaints, such as harmful digital communications notices, handled within the legal time limits.

parts.name: Legal duties for hosts
parts.what: What each country requires hosts to remove, starting with New Zealand, how fast and by whom.

parts.name: Legal notice handling
parts.what: Tracks legal complaints and counter-notices against their deadlines.

parts.name: Law enforcement requests
parts.what: A published process for police and court requests, checked by a lawyer.

features.name: Be protected from known illegal content
features.does: Have known illegal images and videos blocked and reported as the law requires.

parts.name: Safety tooling
parts.what: Known-illegal-content matching, age checks and reporting, with licences and legal duties.

parts.name: Known-content matching
parts.what: Checks uploads against approved hash lists and reports matches to the right agency.

features.name: Be protected from spam
features.does: Have spam and message floods slowed down without blocking real people.

parts.name: Spam limits
parts.what: Limits on new accounts' messages, links and listings, relaxed as trust grows, set as rules on the shared limiter.

features.name: Be protected from scams and fake accounts
features.does: Have scams, fake accounts and off-app payment tricks caught early.

parts.name: Scam methods
parts.what: Proven methods other marketplaces use to stop scams, and what fits a co-op.

parts.name: Fraud signals
parts.what: The one fraud signals service for every app, such as new-account patterns, under published rules, which payment risk rules, scam warnings, fake review checks and faked location flags all feed and read.

parts.name: Reused photo checks
parts.what: Checks new listing and portfolio photos against photos already used elsewhere on Spareware, and sends any match to a person to review. Spare Rent, Spare Market and Spare Work need it.

parts.name: Scam guides
parts.what: Short plain advice on spotting common scams, shown where people need it in each app. Spare Rent and Spare Market both need it.

features.name: Filter what I see by label
features.does: Have content labelled, including AI-made content, and choose what I see.

parts.name: Content labels
parts.what: Labels on posts and listings, set by authors, moderators and checks.

parts.name: Personal filters
parts.what: Hides or blurs labelled content by each person's own choice.

features.name: Know serious bans follow due process
features.does: Have a serious ban apply in every app, only for published reasons and with a right of appeal.

parts.name: Restrictions across apps
parts.what: Restrictions that follow a person across apps only for serious, published reasons.

features.name: Read transparency reports
features.does: Read regular reports on reports, removals, appeals and legal requests.

parts.name: Transparency reports
parts.what: Builds regular reports on reports, removals, appeals and legal requests from the operation log, through the public reporting pipeline.

features.name: Be checked on when something looks wrong
features.does: Get a check-in when a trip stops for a long time or leaves its route.

parts.name: Trip check-ins
parts.what: Spots long stops and route changes and asks whether all is well.

features.name: Let safety groups flag content
features.does: Let recognised safety groups flag content for faster review.

parts.name: Trusted flaggers
parts.what: A priority queue for recognised safety organisations.

features.name: Report sexual harm safely
features.does: Report sexual harm to a trained person, stay in control of what happens next, and be referred to specialist support.

parts.name: Sexual harm response design
parts.what: How specialist services and other platforms handle sexual harm reports: trauma-informed steps, responder training and referral partners in each country.

parts.name: Sexual harm path
parts.what: A separate, trauma-informed report path handled only by trained responders, with referral to support and the reporter choosing whether police are told.

features.name: Be treated fairly whoever I am
features.does: Know every member, worker and customer alike, has agreed not to discriminate, and that patterns of discrimination are checked.

parts.name: Non-discrimination commitment
parts.what: A commitment every member accepts at sign-up under each country's human rights law (example: New Zealand's Human Rights Act 1993), covering how workers treat customers and how customers treat workers.

parts.name: Assistance animal rule
parts.what: One rule for every app that assistance dogs are always accepted and never charged as pets, checked by a lawyer in each country (example: New Zealand's Dog Control Act 1996 and Human Rights Act 1993; *unverified* per app).

features.name: Trust that moderators are consistent and impartial
features.does: Know a sample of moderator and panel decisions gets a second review, and that moderators declare conflicts.

parts.name: Decision sampling and conflict checks
parts.what: Sends a random sample of decisions for a second review, publishes how often they agree, and checks moderators for conflicts of interest.

features.name: Report copied or fake listings
features.does: Report a listing that copies my photos, misuses my trade mark or sells fake goods.

parts.name: Copyright and counterfeit rules
parts.what: What copyright and trade mark law ask of a host that receives notices, including each country's rules for online hosts and counterfeit goods (example: New Zealand's Copyright Act).

parts.name: Copyright and trade mark notices
parts.what: Notices and counter-notices for copied photos, trade mark misuse and counterfeit listings, tracked on the legal notice deadlines.

features.name: Know about emergencies where I work
features.does: See Civil Defence and weather warnings for my area, and have fees, ratings and dispatch paused there when disaster strikes.

parts.name: Official alerts
parts.what: Brings in Civil Defence emergency alerts and MetService warnings for each service area on each source's published terms (MetService's data terms *unverified*), and shows them to people there.

parts.name: Disaster mode
parts.what: A switch for an affected zone that waives cancellation fees, pauses ratings and dispatch there and tells workers in the zone, with each use logged and reported.

features.name: Know about recalled products
features.does: Know when something listed or bought is on a product or food recall list.

parts.name: Recall feeds
parts.what: Brings in government product and food recall lists, starting with New Zealand's, on each source's terms. Spare Market and Spare Food both need them.

parts.name: Recall matching
parts.what: Matches recalls to live listings and past orders by product, brand and model, pulls matching listings and tells buyers.

areas.name: Disputes and appeals
areas.summary: When a job goes wrong the money stays held, both sides are heard, a panel of trained members decides, and either side can appeal. Built as svc-trust.

features.name: Open a dispute
features.does: Raise a problem with an order and have the payout paused until it is settled.

parts.name: Disputes service
parts.what: Disputes linked to orders, with categories, deadlines and status.

parts.name: Dispute form
parts.what: Explains what can be disputed and asks only what is needed.

features.name: Add evidence
features.does: Add photos, messages and the job record to a dispute.

parts.name: Evidence store
parts.what: Gathers order records, chat, trip trace and uploads, with access kept to the parties and the panel.

features.name: Settle it between us first
features.does: Offer or accept a fix, such as a part refund, before a panel is needed.

parts.name: Settlement offers
parts.what: Offers and acceptances that move the held money straight away.

parts.name: Mediation
parts.what: Offers mediation by a trained member, or an outside mediator at cost, before a panel decides. Spare Work and Spare Rent both map it.

features.name: Have a member panel decide
features.does: Have trained members, drawn at random, decide the dispute and give reasons.

parts.name: Panel selection
parts.what: Draws eligible members at random, checks for conflicts of interest and keeps panels balanced.

parts.name: Panel workspace
parts.what: Lets panel members read the evidence, discuss and record a decision.

parts.name: Panel pay
parts.what: Pay for panel time, paid out at cost, with training and certificates from the shared training module.

parts.name: Tax on member role pay
parts.what: How pay to panel members, moderators and ledger checkers is taxed and treated, such as honoraria under New Zealand's schedular payment rules (*unverified*).

parts.name: Legal standing of panel decisions
parts.what: What a panel decision binds and how it sits beside each country's small claims and consumer rights. In New Zealand, the first country pack, that means the Disputes Tribunal and Consumer Guarantees Act rights, and a consumer is bound to arbitration only by a separate written agreement made after the dispute arises (Arbitration Act 1996 s 11).

features.name: Appeal a decision
features.does: Appeal a dispute or moderation decision to a fresh panel.

parts.name: Appeals
parts.what: A second review by different members within set times, run through the one review queue.

features.name: Know how long each step takes
features.does: See each step's deadline and get reminders.

parts.name: Dispute clocks
parts.what: Deadlines for each step, with reminders and a set outcome if time runs out.

features.name: Take it further if needed
features.does: Learn how to take a dispute to a tribunal or regulator if I am not satisfied.

parts.name: Outside routes
parts.what: Plain guidance on tribunals and regulators for each app and country.

parts.name: Evidence pack export
parts.what: Builds a dated evidence pack from the order, messages, photos and decisions as an accessible PDF for a tribunal, a regulator or an insurer. Spare Rent, Spare Market and Spare Work need it.

features.name: See how disputes are decided
features.does: See how many disputes each app had and how they were decided.

parts.name: Dispute statistics
parts.what: Published, anonymous counts and outcomes for each app, through the public reporting pipeline.

features.name: Claim on insurance
features.does: Start an insurance claim from a dispute where an app carries cover.

parts.name: Insurance options
parts.what: Shared cover options across apps, such as a co-op pool or outside insurers, with costs.

parts.name: Insurance claims link
parts.what: Passes dispute evidence to an insurer for apps that carry cover.

parts.name: Income cover options
parts.what: Options for income cover beyond public accident cover (example: New Zealand's ACC), such as an optional group policy at cost, what each covers and what it costs. Spare Food and Spare Ride both map it.

features.name: Be covered by a protection pool
features.does: Claim from a shared protection pool when a buyer, host or customer loses out and the rules cover it.

parts.name: Protection pool rules
parts.what: What the pool covers, how it is funded and how claims are decided, and whether a member-funded pool counts as insurance business under insurance law (example: New Zealand's Insurance (Prudential Supervision) Act 2010; *unverified*).

parts.name: Protection pool
parts.what: One pool service, its money held by the payment provider, with published rules, claims decided through disputes and its own ledger lines for money in and claims paid.

areas.name: Member voting and meetings
areas.summary: Workers propose, discuss and vote on their own app's fees and rules, and members vote on major changes for the whole co-op. Members elect directors, panels and moderators, follow decisions through, and hold meetings online, with a way to vote without a device. One member, one vote. Built as svc-voting.

features.name: Make a proposal
features.does: Propose a change to an app's fees or rules, with my reasons and the exact change.

parts.name: Proposals service
parts.what: Proposals with text, the exact settings change, supporters and status.

parts.name: Proposal editor
parts.what: Write a proposal, preview its effect and gather supporters.

features.name: Discuss before voting
features.does: Discuss a proposal and suggest amendments before the vote opens.

parts.name: Discussion and amendments
parts.what: Threaded discussion and amendments linked to a proposal.

features.name: Vote
features.does: Cast one vote on each proposal I am eligible for.

parts.name: Ballots
parts.what: One member, one vote, with eligibility from the member register and each app's electorate.

parts.name: Voting screen
parts.what: A plain voting screen with the proposal summary and the effect of each choice.

parts.name: Secret and checkable votes
parts.what: How to keep each vote secret while letting members check the count.

parts.name: Vote without a device
parts.what: Postal or phone voting for members without a device, counted with the app votes and checked against the register.

features.name: See results take effect
features.does: See the result, and have a passed change applied to the app automatically.

parts.name: Results to settings
parts.what: Turns a passed vote into the operation that changes the app's fees or rules.

parts.name: Results page
parts.what: Turnout, quorum, the result and exactly what changed.

parts.name: Competition law check
parts.what: Whether worker-members who are contractors may vote together on fares, prices or fees without making a cartel provision under competition law, starting with New Zealand's Commerce Act, and whether a collective bargaining route proposed there in late 2025 now applies (*unverified*).

parts.name: Legal duty locks
parts.what: Marks settings that carry a legal duty, such as a required check, sales tax collection or a notice period, so a passed vote cannot switch them off, and sends any proposal that touches them for legal review before the vote opens.

features.name: Know who votes on what
features.does: See the quorum, timing and who may vote for each kind of decision.

parts.name: Voting rules in the constitution
parts.what: Quorum, notice periods and electorates written into the constitution and rules.

parts.name: Electorates
parts.what: Who votes on what: each app's workers, each app's customer-members, every member, or the board, with what customer-members vote on stated for each app.

features.name: Elect people
features.does: Stand for or vote in elections for directors, panel members and moderators.

parts.name: Elections
parts.what: Nominations, candidate statements and ranked voting.

parts.name: Independent count
parts.what: An independent returning officer or scrutineer for board elections, and a published audit of each count.

parts.name: Candidate checks and consent
parts.what: Checks that each board candidate is not disqualified under company law (example: New Zealand's Companies Act 1993) and holds their written consent before the election opens.

parts.name: Election challenges
parts.what: A route to challenge an election result within a set time, decided by the independent returning officer or as the constitution sets.

features.name: Attend the annual meeting online
features.does: Join the annual meeting online, follow the agenda and vote on motions.

parts.name: Meetings
parts.what: Notices, agendas, motions, attendance and minutes.

parts.name: Meeting video
parts.what: Live video for meetings on the kit's own call service.

features.name: Vote early or by proxy
features.does: Vote before a meeting, or appoint a proxy where the rules allow.

parts.name: Early and proxy votes
parts.what: Records early votes and proxies under the constitution's rules.

features.name: Call a vote or meeting
features.does: Gather enough members to call a vote or a special meeting.

parts.name: Member petitions
parts.what: Collects support towards the number that calls a vote or meeting.

features.name: Share out a budget together
features.does: Divide a budget between projects by member vote.

parts.name: Budget votes
parts.what: Spending choices voted on with points or ranked choices.

features.name: Follow decisions through and answer surveys
features.does: See decisions that need work tracked to done, and answer consultations and surveys that do not bind.

parts.name: Decision tracker
parts.what: Passed decisions that need work rather than a settings change, such as building something or changing a supplier, with an owner, progress and a report back.

parts.name: Consultations and surveys
parts.what: Non-binding questions and surveys to members, with results published and kept apart from binding votes.

areas.name: Open cost ledger
areas.summary: Every month each app publishes what it cost to run, what the fee paid for and how the next fee is set, checked and signed off by members. It also keeps the co-op's own books and runs one pipeline for every public report. Built as svc-ledger.

features.name: See what each app cost
features.does: See each app's costs for the month, line by line.

parts.name: Ledger design
parts.what: What the ledger publishes and how it is checked, with a sample month and who signs it off.

parts.name: Ledger service
parts.what: Cost entries for each app and period, as operations linked to the bills behind them.

parts.name: Ledger pages
parts.what: Public pages and charts for each app and month.

parts.name: Ledger privacy rules
parts.what: Groups staff pay so no one's salary shows, and handles supplier terms that forbid publishing prices, while every dollar still adds up.

features.name: Have bills brought in without retyping
features.does: Have hosting, provider and insurance bills brought into the ledger.

parts.name: Bill imports
parts.what: Pulls bills from hosting and provider accounts, with manual entry for the rest.

parts.name: Usage metering
parts.what: Measures each app's use of shared servers so shared costs are split fairly.

parts.name: Per-account metering
parts.what: Measures each person's and organisation's use of storage, mail, meeting minutes, AI compute and transfer, beside the per-app metering, for apps that price by use.

parts.name: Shared cost split rule
parts.what: A published, member-voted rule for splitting costs that cannot be metered, such as staff, legal, board and audit, between apps.

features.name: See how the fee is set
features.does: See how last period's costs divided by its jobs became this period's fee.

parts.name: Fee setting
parts.what: Works out each app's next fee from its costs, its jobs, the reserve line and any surplus carried forward.

parts.name: Fee explainer
parts.what: Shows how the period's fee was set, with last period's costs, jobs, reserve and any surplus as real figures, linked from each job's fee breakdown.

parts.name: Launch cost estimate
parts.what: What the kit and the first app will cost to run each month at launch, line by line, as the basis for the first fee.

parts.name: Start-up fee rule
parts.what: Sets the fee for the first period, when there is no last period, from the launch estimate, and trues it up once real costs are known.

parts.name: Reserve line
parts.what: A published reserve for chargeback losses, legal costs and insurance excess, set by member vote and shown as its own cost line.

parts.name: Prices by use
parts.what: Works out at-cost prices per unit of use, such as a gigabyte stored or a meeting minute, from the ledger's costs, for apps that have no jobs to divide by.

parts.name: Free allowances and hardship rule
parts.what: Free allowances set by member vote and a published rule for people who cannot pay, with the cost of both shown as a ledger line.

features.name: Check and sign off a month
features.does: As a member chosen for the job, check the month's figures and sign them off.

parts.name: Sign-off workflow
parts.what: Two or more chosen members review, question and sign each month.

features.name: Download the ledger
features.does: Download the ledger as open data.

parts.name: Open data export
parts.what: Publishes each month in CSV and JSON with a stable layout.

features.name: Ask about a cost
features.does: Ask a question about any cost line and see the answer.

parts.name: Ledger questions
parts.what: Questions and answers attached to ledger lines.

features.name: See uptime next to the costs
features.does: See uptime and outages next to what was spent.

parts.name: Uptime in the ledger
parts.what: Adds uptime and incident summaries to each month.

features.name: See next period's budget
features.does: See expected costs and the planned fee before a period starts.

parts.name: Budgets and forecasts
parts.what: Expected costs and fees, compared with the actual figures afterwards.

features.name: Find every public report in one place
features.does: Find the ledger, removals, disputes, support figures and fairness checks published together as open data.

parts.name: Public reporting pipeline
parts.what: One pipeline that builds every public report from the operation log, strips personal details and publishes them with the ledger as open data.

parts.name: Small-number suppression
parts.what: Hides or groups any count in a public report small enough to identify a person, such as one app, place and month, under one published minimum.

features.name: Claim expenses
features.does: As a member or volunteer, claim an expense with a receipt and be paid back once it is approved.

parts.name: Expense claims
parts.what: Claims with receipts, approval by someone other than the claimant, and repayment, each shown in the ledger.

features.name: Keep the co-op's own books
features.does: Trust that the co-op keeps proper books, pays its staff and suppliers, and has its yearly accounts audited.

parts.name: Bookkeeping system choice
parts.what: Compares existing accounting systems on sales tax (example: New Zealand GST), bank feeds, payroll links, licence and cost, so the co-op uses one rather than building its own.

parts.name: Books link
parts.what: Feeds ledger costs, fee income and payouts owed into the co-op's accounts and reconciles them with the bank.

parts.name: Supplier bills and staff pay
parts.what: Approves and pays supplier bills, and pays staff through the one payroll provider link, each payment an operation with two people signing off.

parts.name: Yearly accounts and audit
parts.what: The financial statements and audit the law and the constitution require, with the auditor chosen by members.

features.name: Fund the start
features.does: Give a donation, a grant or a member loan to fund the co-op before fees cover its costs, and see how it was spent.

parts.name: Funding rules
parts.what: How the co-op may take donations, grants and member loans, including securities law for member loans, tax on donations and anti-money-laundering checks.

parts.name: Funding records
parts.what: Takes donations, grants and member loans through the payment provider, records each on the ledger with its terms, and shows how it was spent and what is owed back.

areas.name: Co-op membership and member portal
areas.summary: The co-op's own home: joining for free once per person, the member register, member roles, refunds of any fees above running costs, reports, the constitution, discipline, board work, insurance, contributors' rights, the steward society and the federation of local co-ops. Proposed as svc-members (KIT-A16-F10-P1); the member register feeds svc-voting.

features.name: Join the co-op
features.does: Become a member for free by taking part with a Spareware account and agreeing to the constitution, with no shares and no joining fee.

parts.name: Legal entity
parts.what: The legal form of the operating co-op and of the steward that holds the code and name.

parts.name: Free membership terms
parts.what: Confirms free membership, with no shares and no fee, is not a securities offer and needs no disclosure document.

parts.name: Join flow
parts.what: Explains membership, which is free, and records acceptance of the constitution.

parts.name: One person, one membership
parts.what: An identity check and a duplicate check before membership starts, so no one holds two memberships or two votes.

parts.name: Business members
parts.what: Restaurants, shops and trade firms join as business members under the constitution's member classes, with a check that the business is real before it joins.

features.name: Be on the member register
features.does: Know my membership is recorded correctly.

parts.name: Member register
parts.what: The member register and member classes for each app, every change an operation.

parts.name: Membership certificate
parts.what: A member number and a downloadable certificate.

parts.name: Active member check
parts.what: Tracks which members take part in each app, so votes stay with people who use it, and flags members who stop taking part.

parts.name: Register inspection
parts.what: Handles requests to inspect the member register where the law for the co-op's legal form allows it (*unverified* scope) without showing members' home addresses beyond what the law requires.

features.name: See my membership at a glance
features.does: See my open votes, roles, earnings and co-op news in one place.

parts.name: Member portal home
parts.what: One page with open votes, my roles, my apps, ledger news and meetings, in Spareware red.

features.name: Read the constitution and reports
features.does: Read the constitution, rules, minutes and annual reports, with past versions.

parts.name: Co-op documents library
parts.what: The versioned constitution, rules, minutes and reports.

parts.name: Yearly filings
parts.what: Annual returns and statements to the company registry (example: New Zealand's Companies Office) and regulators, using the audited yearly accounts.

features.name: Get back fees above running costs
features.does: See any fees I paid above running costs returned to me as a refund or as lower fees.

parts.name: Fee records
parts.what: Records the fees each member paid, as the basis for any refund of fees above running costs.

parts.name: Fee refunds
parts.what: Works out and pays refunds of fees above running costs once members have voted on them.

parts.name: Fee refund tax
parts.what: How fee refunds are taxed and reported for each member.

features.name: Take on a member role
features.does: Volunteer as a panel member, moderator or ledger checker, and get trained.

parts.name: Member roles
parts.what: Role sign-up, terms and conflict of interest declarations, with training and certificates from the shared training module.

features.name: Invite people
features.does: Invite friends or workers to join with a personal link.

parts.name: Invites
parts.what: Personal invite links that count joins without tracking anyone elsewhere.

features.name: Leave the co-op
features.does: Leave whenever I choose, with my votes and roles closed under the constitution.

parts.name: Leaving
parts.what: Ends a membership and closes its votes and roles, keeping the records the law requires.

features.name: Find other members
features.does: Find members who chose to be listed, by app or place.

parts.name: Member directory
parts.what: An opt-in directory showing only what each member chooses.

features.name: Read what other co-ops learned
features.does: Read the study of other platform co-ops and see which of its lessons shaped the kit's rules.

parts.name: Platform co-op study
parts.what: What worked and failed for ride, courier and holiday rental co-ops, with current status.

features.name: Run the board in the open
features.does: As a director, keep board papers, minutes and interests in one place members can check.

parts.name: Board area
parts.what: Board papers, minutes, an interests register and resolutions, with board meetings run on the shared meetings part.

features.name: Start a co-op in another country
features.does: Start or join a local co-op in another country under the shared name and kit.

parts.name: Name licence for local co-ops
parts.what: The steward's licence of the Spareware name to co-ops that keep the rules.

parts.name: Federation register
parts.what: Local co-ops, their regions, members and apps.

features.name: See contributors credited
features.does: See contributions to the code credited to the members who made them.

parts.name: Contributor records
parts.what: Links reviewed contributions to members who choose to show them.

features.name: Have a fair hearing before suspension or expulsion
features.does: Know a member is suspended or expelled only under the constitution, after a hearing, and separately from any app ban.

parts.name: Member discipline rules
parts.what: The constitution's grounds, notice, hearing and appeal for suspending or expelling a member.

parts.name: Suspension and expulsion
parts.what: Notice, hearing, decision and appeal recorded against the register, kept apart from app bans and restrictions.

features.name: Run the steward society
features.does: As a member of the steward society, see its register, committee, annual meeting, accounts and disputes procedure.

parts.name: Steward society rules
parts.what: The constitution, committee, disputes procedure and yearly duties the law requires of the steward (example: New Zealand's Incorporated Societies Act 2022).

parts.name: Steward register and meetings
parts.what: The society's own member register, committee records, annual meeting and financial statements, reusing the co-op's register, meetings and books.

features.name: Contribute with clear rights
features.does: Sign off my contributions with the Developer Certificate of Origin, keep the copyright to my work, and know Spareware will never be relicensed, with my employer's consent where I worked on their time.

parts.name: Contributor sign-off
parts.what: Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off on every commit, with no contributor licence agreement, and employer consent for work done on an employer's time.

parts.name: Sign-off check
parts.what: A repository check that every contribution carries the sign-off before it is merged.

features.name: Know the co-op is insured
features.does: Know the co-op and its board carry the insurance they need, with the cost in the ledger.

parts.name: Co-op insurance
parts.what: Directors and officers, cyber and public liability cover for the co-op across all apps, compared on cost and what each covers.

features.name: Know the name is protected
features.does: Know Spareware's names, domains and accounts are held by the co-op's steward, not by any one person.

parts.name: Trade marks
parts.what: Registers Spareware and the product names as trade marks in each country, starting with the first example country, New Zealand, held by the steward and licensed to local co-ops.

parts.name: Domains held by the steward
parts.what: The steward holds every Spareware domain under two-person control, so no single person can lose or take one.

features.name: Know what happens if an app or the co-op closes
features.does: Know I will get notice, my data and any money owed if an app or the co-op closes.

parts.name: Wind-down plan
parts.what: Notice periods, a data export window, payouts and held money settled, and code and data passed to the steward or members when an app or the co-op closes.

areas.name: Sync, history and storage
areas.summary: The base every app is built on (kit-core, kit-ops, kit-sync, kit-store): permanent IDs, every change as an operation with versioned schemas, personal data that can still be erased, undo, history, offline work, live co-editing, timers that survive restarts, files, previews, shared libraries, a document vault and sharing. Files are served by a file service proposed as svc-files (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Have every change go through one checked path
features.does: Have every change, by a person, an AI agent or an add-in, checked and recorded the same way.

parts.name: Permanent IDs and core types
parts.what: 128-bit time-ordered IDs, units, errors and time types, so offline work never collides; money uses the one shared money type.

parts.name: Commands and operations
parts.what: Commands, checks, transactions and the operation log.

parts.name: Command schemas
parts.what: Each app's commands described once, so the interface, API, plugins and AI share them.

parts.name: Permission checks
parts.what: Checks every operation against who is acting and their roles.

parts.name: Personal data in a permanent log
parts.what: How to erase personal data from an append-only, tamper-evident operation log, such as keeping it outside operations or encrypting it per person and destroying the key.

parts.name: Erasable personal data
parts.what: Builds the chosen method, so deletion, correction and retention work while replay and the financial log stay intact.

parts.name: Operation versions and upgrades
parts.what: A version on every operation schema, upgraders that read old operations as new ones, and migration tests run against recorded history.

parts.name: Snapshots
parts.what: Checked snapshots of state that cap how much history must be replayed to open an app or rebuild a service.

parts.name: Idempotency keys
parts.what: Every command carries a unique key, so a command retried or replayed from an offline queue, an agent, a script or a webhook never books or charges twice, the pattern Stripe's API uses.

features.name: Undo and redo
features.does: Undo and redo my own changes, even in shared work.

parts.name: Undo and redo
parts.what: Undo by inverse operations, kept for each person in shared work.

features.name: See history
features.does: See who changed what and when, and go back to any earlier version.

parts.name: Version history
parts.what: Browse, compare and restore versions from the operation log.

features.name: Work offline
features.does: Keep working without a connection and have it sync when I am back.

parts.name: Sync method
parts.what: Server-ordered operation log or CRDT, covering offline work, conflicts and deterministic replay.

parts.name: Sync engine
parts.what: A server-ordered operation log with offline queues and deterministic replay.

parts.name: Conflict handling
parts.what: Clear rules, and a plain prompt, when offline changes clash.

parts.name: Protected offline data
parts.what: Keeps offline data on phones and computers encrypted, and wipes it when the device is signed out remotely.

parts.name: Autosave and crash recovery
parts.what: Saves work to a local journal as it happens and replays it after a crash or power cut, so a file opens exactly where it was. Spare Studio and Spare Office both need it.

features.name: See changes live
features.does: See other people's changes appear as they make them.

parts.name: Live updates
parts.what: Pushes new operations to every open device.

parts.name: Presence
parts.what: Shows who else is here and what they are working on.

features.name: Open big work quickly
features.does: Open large design files fast, loading only what I am working on.

parts.name: Storage choices
parts.what: Entity store and project file format, covering chunked storage and permanent IDs.

parts.name: Chunked storage
parts.what: Chunks, paging from disk and a spatial index, in a crash-safe container file.

features.name: Add photos and files
features.does: Add photos and files to listings, chats and documents.

parts.name: File uploads
parts.what: Resumable uploads, safety scanning, image sizes and content addressing, kept in object storage by the one file service.

parts.name: Storage at cost
parts.what: Object storage with quotas, and at-cost prices for heavy use.

parts.name: Photo metadata stripping
parts.what: Removes location and other hidden details from uploaded photos, keeping only what the person chooses to share.

parts.name: Photo privacy check
parts.what: Flags faces, number plates, mail, valuables, alarm panels and keys in photos, without identifying anyone, so the person can blur them before the photos go live.

parts.name: When storage lapses
parts.what: Over quota or after non-payment, files turn read-only after long notice, and nothing is deleted without repeated warnings and a window to export.

features.name: Share with people
features.does: Share a file or item with chosen people or a link, and change access at any time.

parts.name: Sharing and access
parts.what: Sharing with people or by link, at view, comment or edit level.

parts.name: Guest access by private link
parts.what: Lets someone with no account, such as a tenant, guarantor or outside guest, open just what was shared with them through a private link and a one-time code, to read, sign or answer. Spare Office, Spare Home and Spare Rent need it.

features.name: Get deleted things back
features.does: Restore deleted items for a set time before they are gone for good.

parts.name: Recycle bin
parts.what: Keeps deleted items for a set time and restores them on request.

features.name: Co-edit text
features.does: Type in the same document as others with no lost work.

parts.name: Text co-editing
parts.what: A text CRDT on the operation log for documents and long text.

features.name: Branch and merge
features.does: Try changes on a branch and merge them back.

parts.name: Branches
parts.what: Branches and merges of operation logs, used most by the design tools.

features.name: Keep my files private
features.does: Have files encrypted so only the people I share with can read them.

parts.name: Encryption choice
parts.what: Where to encrypt at rest and where end to end, and what that costs search and recovery.

features.name: Keep my documents in one place
features.does: Keep the documents for an order, a property or an organisation in one place, with versions, dates and expiry, and share them with the people who need them.

parts.name: Document vault
parts.what: Typed documents with versions, dates, expiry reminders and sharing, attached to an order, a property or an organisation, on the one file service.

features.name: Have things happen on time
features.does: Have auto-confirms, deadlines, reminders and scheduled bookings happen on time, even after a server restarts.

parts.name: Durable timers
parts.what: Timers and scheduled jobs stored as operations, so auto-confirm, dispute clocks, re-checks, scheduled bookings, retention deletion, card hold renewals and payout runs survive restarts and fire once.

features.name: Sync my folders with my computer
features.does: Keep chosen folders on my computer in sync with my Spareware storage.

parts.name: Desktop sync client
parts.what: One desktop client for every program that syncs chosen folders with a person's Spareware storage, handling conflicts and offline changes.

features.name: See a preview of any file
features.does: See a thumbnail or quick preview of any photo, video, document or model without opening its app.

parts.name: Preview service
parts.what: Makes thumbnails and previews for every supported format, such as photos, video, PDF, office files and 3D, in a sandbox, using the shared engines. Spare Office, Spare Studio, Spare Social, Spare OS and Spare Construct need the same service.

features.name: Show work to someone with no app
features.does: Send someone a link to view my work in a browser, with no account or install.

parts.name: Web viewer
parts.what: A read-only browser viewer for PDFs, images, video, audio, layouts, sheets and 3D, with no account or install. Spare Construct and Spare Studio both need it.

features.name: Use shared libraries and templates
features.does: Use libraries of reusable content and templates that my team or the co-op shares.

parts.name: Content library service
parts.what: One versioned library of reusable content, such as families, materials, fonts, brand kits and templates, loaded by reference, with organisation and public collections, stored on the file service and metered to the ledger. Spare Construct and Spare Studio both need it.

parts.name: Template gallery
parts.what: Co-op-made templates kept as normal files with fill-in fields and listed in a gallery, for documents, slides, posters and social posts. Spare Studio and Spare Office both need it.

parts.name: Open collections with licences
parts.what: Collections of materials, textures, sounds and music under open licences, each with its licence and credit recorded and shown. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare Social need them.

areas.name: Plugins, open API and integrations
areas.summary: Everything a person can do, a script or add-in can do: one command API per app, sandboxed plugins (kit-plugin), webhooks, SDKs, a plugin directory and links to outside tools, with limits that stop bulk copying, and named kit parts every program builds on.

features.name: Use every app from a script
features.does: Do anything I can do in an app through its API.

parts.name: Command API
parts.what: A command and query API for each app, generated from the command schemas.

parts.name: API keys and tokens
parts.what: Personal and app tokens with scopes, expiry and revocation.

parts.name: API rate limits
parts.what: Fair, published limits for each token, set as rules on the shared limiter.

parts.name: Bulk copy limits
parts.what: Stops the API and MCP server being used to harvest profiles, addresses and reviews: no bulk lists of personal data, caps per person reached, and alerts on harvesting patterns.

parts.name: Headless parity check
parts.what: A release check that every action on every screen maps to a command in the schema, so anything a person can do, an agent or a script can do too.

features.name: Be told when something changes
features.does: Have my own systems called when an order, payment or message changes.

parts.name: Webhooks
parts.what: Signed webhooks with retries and a delivery log.

features.name: Build with a ready-made library
features.does: Use ready-made libraries for common languages.

parts.name: SDKs
parts.what: One TypeScript library generated from the command schemas at first, with Rust and Python libraries added next.

parts.name: Developer docs
parts.what: Docs, examples and a changelog, generated wherever possible.

parts.name: Test mode
parts.what: A sandbox with test accounts and test payments.

parts.name: Marketplace simulator
parts.what: Runs simulated customers and workers on real map data through the same commands as people, so matching, dispatch, fee setting and fraud rules are measured before launch, with each app adding its own behaviours.

parts.name: Command-line tool
parts.what: One command-line tool generated from each app's command schemas, for scripts, batch conversion and checks from a terminal. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare OS need it.

features.name: Know the licence
features.does: Know the core is under MPL-2.0 and the SDK and plugins under Apache-2.0, and that neither will ever be relicensed.

parts.name: Licence decision
parts.what: The decided licences: MPL-2.0 for the core and Apache-2.0 for the SDK and plugins, never relicensed, with no contributor licence agreement and Developer Certificate of Origin sign-off only.

features.name: Install an add-in
features.does: Add a plugin to an app and see what it will be allowed to do first.

parts.name: Plugin method
parts.what: WebAssembly components on wasmtime: what authors in each language can use today.

parts.name: Plugin host
parts.what: Runs plugins as sandboxed WebAssembly components with declared permissions.

parts.name: Permission prompt
parts.what: Shows a plugin's permissions in plain words before it is installed.

parts.name: Plugin panels
parts.what: Lets plugins add panels and buttons built with HTML and TypeScript, inside the sandbox and with declared permissions. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare Office need them.

features.name: Find add-ins
features.does: Browse, rate and install plugins from one directory.

parts.name: Plugin directory
parts.what: Listings, versions, reviews and install counts.

parts.name: Plugin review and signing
parts.what: Checks and signs plugins before they are listed, with a way to pull a bad one.

features.name: Publish an add-in
features.does: Publish a plugin, and charge a fair price for it if I choose.

parts.name: Publisher tools
parts.what: Upload, versions and usage figures for plugin authors.

parts.name: Paid add-ins
parts.what: Pays plugin authors through the payments service, charging sales tax under each country's remote services and marketplace operator rules and issuing tax invoices.

features.name: Connect outside tools
features.does: Link Spareware to accounting, calendar and other common tools.

parts.name: Common connectors
parts.what: Connectors to widely used tools through their published APIs, on terms that allow it.

features.name: Rely on the API staying stable
features.does: Rely on the API not breaking without notice.

parts.name: Versions and deprecation
parts.what: Versioned APIs with published notice periods before anything is removed.

features.name: Build an app on named kit parts
features.does: As a contributor, depend on a named kit service or crate instead of rebuilding tax, search, support or any other shared part.

parts.name: Kit service and crate catalogue
parts.what: Published names for the kit's eight services and seven crates, the five shared engines mapped in KIT-A27, the new names this map proposes (such as svc-identity, svc-tax, svc-search, svc-support, svc-members, svc-files, svc-translate, kit-ui, kit-i18n, engine-formats and engine-models) until ARCHITECTURE.md adopts them, the part IDs each covers, and the layering rule that kit services may use engines while kit-core never may.

parts.name: Layering check
parts.what: A repository check that flags a program depending on another program, a program mapping its own copy of a part the kit provides, or kit-core depending on an engine.

features.name: Record and replay my actions
features.does: Record what I do once and replay it, on one file or many.

parts.name: Action recorder
parts.what: Records a person's operations as a script they can edit, replay and run on many files. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare Office need the same recorder.

features.name: Run scripts inside an app
features.does: Write, run and fix a script next to the work it changes.

parts.name: Script console
parts.what: A console and editor inside each app to write, run and debug scripts against its command API, with time and memory limits. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare Office need it.

features.name: Write formulas safely
features.does: Write a formula or expression that can never harm my file or my computer.

parts.name: Safe expression language
parts.what: A small, sandboxed expression language with units checked and a library of common functions, for parameter formulas and animation expressions. Spare Construct and Spare Studio both need it.

areas.name: AI access
areas.summary: Lets members use AI agents with every app through the same commands as people (kit-mcp), with permissions they choose, approval for money, guards against hidden instructions, agent actions labelled to the other side, people-only votes and reviews, and a record of everything an agent did.

features.name: Connect my AI agent
features.does: Connect an AI agent to any Spareware app and choose what it may do.

parts.name: MCP server
parts.what: An MCP server for each app, built from its command schemas.

parts.name: Agent sign-in
parts.what: Agents sign in through the sign-in service with the scopes the person picks.

parts.name: MCP authorisation
parts.what: Meets the MCP authorisation spec: OAuth 2.1 with PKCE S256, protected resource metadata (RFC 9728), audience-bound tokens (RFC 8707), refresh token rotation and client ID metadata documents.

features.name: Approve important actions
features.does: Approve any payment, booking or step that can't be undone before an agent takes it.

parts.name: Approval steps
parts.what: Marks the commands that need a person's approval and asks for it.

features.name: See what an agent did
features.does: See every action an agent took, and undo it.

parts.name: Agent activity
parts.what: Lists agent actions from the operation log, with undo.

features.name: Keep agents within limits
features.does: Set spending, rate and scope limits for each agent.

parts.name: Agent limits
parts.what: Spending, rate and scope limits for each agent.

features.name: Protect my agent from hidden instructions
features.does: Have agents protected from instructions hidden in listings, messages or documents.

parts.name: Hidden instruction guards
parts.what: Marks outside content as data and limits what an agent can do with it.

features.name: Choose the AI model
features.does: Bring my own AI, or use one the co-op runs at cost.

parts.name: AI tools policy
parts.what: Options for models, cost and consent, shared with Spare Studio.

parts.name: Co-op AI at cost
parts.what: Open models run by the co-op and charged at cost.

features.name: Ask an assistant for help
features.does: Ask an assistant how to do something in any app.

parts.name: Help assistant
parts.what: Answers from the help centre and acts only with approval.

features.name: Use an app by voice
features.does: Run an app hands-free by voice, such as while driving.

parts.name: Voice control
parts.what: Voice commands mapped to the same commands as the interface.

features.name: Know when I am dealing with an agent
features.does: See when a message, offer or booking came from someone's AI agent, and know votes and reviews come only from people.

parts.name: Agent labels
parts.what: Marks every message, offer and booking an agent makes, so the other side sees it came from an agent acting for a named person.

parts.name: People-only actions
parts.what: Ratings, reviews, votes, elections, proxies, dispute statements, signing agreements, accepting terms, joining or leaving the co-op, and consenting to biometric or background checks can be done only by the person, never by an agent.

features.name: See where the co-op uses AI
features.does: See every place the co-op uses AI to shape a decision about me, and ask for a person to review it.

parts.name: AI use register
parts.what: A public register of where AI is used, such as moderation hints, matching, support and translation, with what each model may decide.

parts.name: Human review of AI decisions
parts.what: Lets a member ask for a person to review any decision an automated tool shaped, through the one review queue.

features.name: Choose whether my data trains AI
features.does: Choose whether my data or work is ever used to train an AI model, with the answer no until I say yes.

parts.name: AI training choice
parts.what: A choice, off by default, over whether a member's data or work is used to train any AI model, kept in the consent records and checked before every training run.

features.name: Let my agent pay under a mandate I signed
features.does: Let my agent pay within a mandate I signed, which the payment provider and the other side can check.

parts.name: Signed payment mandates
parts.what: Agent payments under a signed mandate the person approved, which the provider and the other side can check, on an open protocol such as AP2 where the provider supports it.

features.name: Run an agent for my organisation
features.does: Run an AI agent for my restaurant, shop or office, with permissions set for the organisation and a named owner.

parts.name: Organisation agents
parts.what: Agents that act for an organisation, with organisation-wide permissions and limits, and a named person who owns each one.

areas.name: Privacy, data rights and legal duties
areas.summary: Members see, take and delete their data, consent is recorded, data is kept only as long as needed, a named privacy officer answers, overseas handling is checked, indigenous data, such as Māori data, is cared for, and the co-op meets privacy, consumer and platform law in each country through its country pack, starting with New Zealand. Built in svc-accounts; svc-privacy is a proposed name (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Download all my data
features.does: Download everything held about me, from every app, in open formats.

parts.name: Data export
parts.what: Exports everything held about a person in documented open formats: profile, orders, messages, ratings, files, support cases, decisions about them, check results, consents, agent activity and, where the law allows, risk flags.

features.name: Delete my account
features.does: Delete my account and data, apart from what the law says must be kept.

parts.name: Account deletion
parts.what: Deletes or anonymises data across services, keeping legally required records apart.

parts.name: Settle up before closing
parts.what: Before an account closes, ends or cancels open orders, settles money owed either way, closes open disputes and checks legal holds, in that order.

features.name: See and correct my data
features.does: See what is held about me and who accessed it, and ask to correct it.

parts.name: Privacy page
parts.what: Shows the data held, who accessed it, and correction requests.

parts.name: Privacy request clock
parts.what: Tracks every request to see or correct personal information against each country's time limit (example: 20 working days under New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020), with reminders and any extension recorded.

features.name: Agree to terms I can read
features.does: Read short terms, see what changed, and know what I agreed to.

parts.name: Terms and policy versions
parts.what: Versioned terms and policies, with a record of each person's acceptance.

parts.name: Terms and privacy policy
parts.what: Plain terms and a privacy policy for each app, checked by a lawyer.

features.name: Be told what is collected about me
features.does: Be told what is collected and why, including data that comes from someone else.

parts.name: Collection notices
parts.what: Notices for direct and indirect collection under each country's privacy law (example: New Zealand's Privacy Act, including principle 3A from 1 May 2026).

features.name: Know data is kept only as long as needed
features.does: Know data is deleted on a published schedule.

parts.name: Retention schedules
parts.what: Retention rules for each kind of data, legal holds and automatic deletion.

features.name: Be told about a breach
features.does: Be told quickly if my data is exposed.

parts.name: Breach response
parts.what: Breach assessment and notification to the privacy regulator (example: New Zealand's Privacy Commissioner) and the people affected.

features.name: Get the protection consumer law gives
features.does: Get my consumer law rights in every app.

parts.name: Consumer law for platforms
parts.what: Fair trading, consumer guarantees and unfair contract terms duties for each app.

features.name: Keep my data in my region
features.does: Have my data stored in my region where the law asks.

parts.name: Data location
parts.what: Places each member's data by region and records where it is kept.

features.name: Trust that new features are checked for privacy
features.does: Know every new feature is checked for privacy before it ships.

parts.name: Privacy impact assessments
parts.what: A short template and a public register of assessments.

features.name: Have my account handled after I die
features.does: Let a named person close or keep my account after my death.

parts.name: After-death account handling
parts.what: A named contact and a process to close, keep or hand over an account.

features.name: Have overseas privacy rights honoured
features.does: Have the rights other countries' privacy laws give me honoured.

parts.name: Overseas privacy duties
parts.what: Duties under laws such as the EU's GDPR for each country added.

features.name: Have overseas platform law met
features.does: Have overseas platform duties, such as notice and appeal rules, met.

parts.name: Overseas platform duties
parts.what: Duties under laws such as the EU Digital Services Act and the UK Online Safety Act.

features.name: Reach the privacy officer
features.does: Contact the named privacy officer for the co-op or any app about my data.

parts.name: Privacy officer
parts.what: Appoints a named privacy officer for the co-op and every app, as privacy law requires (example: New Zealand's Privacy Act 2020), reachable from every privacy page.

features.name: Know who else handles my data
features.does: See which outside services handle my data, what they do with it and which countries it goes to.

parts.name: Overseas disclosure checks
parts.what: Checks under information privacy principle 12 before personal data goes to an overseas provider, such as the payment provider, push, email and text services.

parts.name: Processor list
parts.what: A published list of every outside processor, what it handles and where, updated whenever one changes.

features.name: Have indigenous data cared for
features.does: Know indigenous language data, voice recordings and community data are cared for under indigenous data sovereignty principles, such as Māori data sovereignty in New Zealand.

parts.name: Indigenous data principles
parts.what: How indigenous data sovereignty principles apply to language data, voice and community data in each country, starting with Māori data sovereignty principles in New Zealand, such as Te Mana Raraunga's, for te reo Māori and iwi-related data, worked through with Māori members.

features.name: See and change every consent I gave
features.does: See every consent I gave, such as for marketing, location or AI use, and withdraw any of them in one step.

parts.name: Consent records
parts.what: One service that records each consent, such as marketing, biometrics, background checks, location, AI use and crash reports, with its version and time, and that every app checks before use.

parts.name: Consents page
parts.what: Shows every consent a person gave, in every app, and withdraws any of them in one step.

features.name: Have sensitive details handled with care
features.does: Have my health, religious and disability details asked for only when needed and kept with extra care.

parts.name: Sensitive details rules
parts.what: Rules for health, religious and disability details: consent before saving, the least detail each party needs, no use in suggestions unless switched on, one-step deletion, and special category treatment where the GDPR applies. Spare Food, Spare Ride and Spare Office need them.

parts.name: Health information rules
parts.what: What the Health Information Privacy Code 2020 asks when health details are kept, such as rides booked for patients or health providers using office tools.

areas.name: Languages, accessibility and countries
areas.summary: Every app works in many languages from the start, beginning with the example country's (for New Zealand: English and te reo Māori), meets accessibility standards, gets each country's holidays, time zones and emergency numbers right through its country pack, and takes on new languages and countries without rewriting. Proposed as kit-i18n and svc-translate (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Use an app in my language
features.does: Switch any app between many languages, starting with the example country's (for New Zealand: English and te reo Māori).

parts.name: Translation framework
parts.what: The one translation framework every app uses: message strings with plural and gender rules, in an open format such as Fluent.

parts.name: Local formats
parts.what: Dates, numbers, money and addresses for each locale, using ICU4X.

parts.name: Member translation
parts.what: A workflow for member translators, with reviewers for each language.

parts.name: Macron-aware matching
parts.what: Matching that ignores macrons when people type, so Maori finds Māori in search and addresses.

parts.name: Community languages
parts.what: Chooses and funds the next languages members speak most, starting in the first example country, New Zealand, with languages such as Samoan, Tongan, Chinese and Hindi, translated with fluent speakers once for every app. Spare OS, Spare Home, Spare Rent, Spare Work and Spare Market all plan them.

parts.name: Translated listing fields
parts.what: Lets authors write or correct their own translations of names and descriptions, shown in each reader's language and found by search. Spare Social, Spare Food and Spare Stay need it.

features.name: Use every screen with a screen reader or keyboard
features.does: Use every screen with a screen reader, a keyboard or a switch.

parts.name: Accessible components
parts.what: Shared components built and tested to WCAG 2.2 AA.

parts.name: Accessibility testing
parts.what: Automatic checks plus testing with disabled members before each release.

parts.name: Image descriptions
parts.what: Asks for a description when an image is added, so screen readers can read it.

parts.name: Accessibility statement and barrier reports
parts.what: An accessibility statement for each app and a way to report a barrier, answered through support within a published time, as the European Accessibility Act asks of online shops and transport services.

parts.name: Accessibility conformance reports
parts.what: A published conformance report for each app against WCAG 2.2 and EN 301 549, updated each release. Spare Studio, Spare Office and Spare OS need them.

parts.name: Accessibility checker for content
parts.what: Checks documents and designs against WCAG 2.2 and PDF/UA, such as contrast, missing alt text and reading order, with a fix for each issue. Spare Office and Spare Studio need the same checker.

parts.name: Canvas mirror for screen readers
parts.what: A hidden structure that tells screen readers what is drawn on a canvas, such as pages, sheets, slides, layers and selections. Spare Office and Spare Studio share one.

parts.name: Accessibility law research
parts.what: Which accessibility laws apply to each app in each country, such as New Zealand's rules and the EU's European Accessibility Act, and what each requires. Spare OS, Spare Studio and Spare Stay all ask.

features.name: Make text and colours easy to read
features.does: Make text larger, raise contrast and reduce motion.

parts.name: Display settings
parts.what: Text size, contrast and motion settings that follow the device.

features.name: Get captions and transcripts
features.does: Get captions and transcripts on videos and voice messages.

parts.name: Captions
parts.what: Captions and transcripts for media, shared with Spare Social.

features.name: Use an app on an old phone or a slow connection
features.does: Use apps on older phones and weak connections.

parts.name: Light mode for slow connections
parts.what: Smaller pages, fewer images and screens that work offline first.

features.name: Use an app in a new country
features.does: Use an app in another country with its money, taxes, laws and ID checks.

parts.name: Country packs
parts.what: Packs for each new country in the format the first pack, New Zealand, sets: currency, tax, ID providers, emergency numbers, helplines, holidays and legal rules.

features.name: Read right to left
features.does: Use the apps in right-to-left languages.

parts.name: Right-to-left layout
parts.what: Mirrored layouts and right-to-left text handling.

features.name: Read an easy version
features.does: Read key screens and rules in easy-read and sign language versions (for New Zealand: New Zealand Sign Language).

parts.name: Easy read and sign language
parts.what: Easy-read text and videos in each country's sign language, starting with New Zealand Sign Language, for the key steps in each app.

features.name: Have each country's dates and numbers right from day one
features.does: Have deadlines, notice periods and emergency numbers follow each country's real calendar, holidays and time zones, starting with New Zealand's.

parts.name: First country pack (example: New Zealand)
parts.what: The first country pack, New Zealand, which sets the format every other pack follows: the emergency number and 111 TXT, helplines, GST rate, currency, public holidays including Matariki and regional anniversary days, and both time zones including the Chatham Islands.

parts.name: Working days and notice periods
parts.what: Counts working days, public holidays and notice periods for legal clocks, dispute deadlines, meeting notices and tax due dates.

features.name: Read translations made at cost
features.does: Read messages, listings and help pages machine-translated by one co-op service, with each language, such as te reo Māori, checked by fluent speakers.

parts.name: Translation model choice
parts.what: Compares open translation models whose licences allow this use, on quality for each language, such as te reo Māori, and on running cost.

parts.name: Machine translation at cost
parts.what: One translation service for every app, run at cost, that labels machine translations and keeps the original one tap away.

parts.name: Translation quality checks
parts.what: Fluent members review samples of translations in each language, such as te reo Māori, and weak language pairs are switched off until they pass.

features.name: Read receipts and statements with a screen reader
features.does: Read every receipt, statement, invoice and certificate with a screen reader.

parts.name: Accessible PDFs
parts.what: Tagged, accessible PDFs for receipts, statements, invoices and certificates.

features.name: Use a simpler layout
features.does: Switch to a pared-back layout with large text and only the main tasks.

parts.name: Simple mode
parts.what: A pared-back layout with the main tasks first and large text, for people new to an app. Spare Ride and Spare Market both plan it.

areas.name: App shell and phone apps
areas.summary: The shared frame every app runs in: components from the design guide, installable phone and desktop apps, push, deep links, settings and moving between Spareware apps. Proposed as kit-ui (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Use apps that look and work alike
features.does: Find the same buttons and screens in every Spareware app.

parts.name: Shared interface components
parts.what: HTML and TypeScript components built on the design guide and its tokens.

parts.name: App frame
parts.what: Header, navigation, account menu and each app's own colour.

parts.name: Licences and credits screen
parts.what: A screen in every app listing each open-source library and asset used, with its licence notice and source, generated from the dependency checks.

features.name: Install an app on my phone
features.does: Install an app on a phone and get push and location like any other app.

parts.name: Phone app approach
parts.what: Web apps, Tauri mobile or native, covering live location, push and app store rules.

parts.name: Installable apps
parts.what: The chosen phone and desktop wrappers for every app.

parts.name: Location and background permissions
parts.what: Asks for location and background use only when needed, explained in plain words.

parts.name: Desktop shell choice
parts.what: A decision note on the desktop wrapper, such as Tauri or our own web view host, with native code in the same process for heavy apps. Spare Construct, Spare Office, Spare Studio and Spare Social need the same shell.

parts.name: Desktop installers
parts.what: Signed installers for Windows, macOS and Linux that add or remove single apps, with automatic updates and roll back. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare Office need them.

parts.name: Battery and data budgets
parts.what: Published limits on battery and data use over a full shift for worker apps, tested on common phones, with fewer location updates while waiting. Spare Ride and Spare Food both need them.

features.name: Move between apps
features.does: Move between Spareware apps without signing in again.

parts.name: App switcher
parts.what: Lists the apps I use and opens each with my account.

features.name: Open a link in the right place
features.does: Open a shared link straight to the listing, order or chat it points to.

parts.name: Deep links
parts.what: Links that open the right screen in the app or the browser.

features.name: Change my settings
features.does: Find every setting for my account and each app in one place.

parts.name: Settings framework
parts.what: Shared settings pages that each app adds to.

parts.name: Preferences that follow me
parts.what: Typed preferences per person, organisation and project, with a clear order of which wins, saved as operations so they reach every device and can be exported. Spare Construct, Spare Studio, Spare Office and Spare Ride need them.

features.name: Get started quickly
features.does: Learn what an app does in a short first-run guide.

parts.name: First-run guide
parts.what: Short intro screens and helpful empty pages in each app.

parts.name: Tips in context
parts.what: Short tips on a tool or setting the first time it is used, which can be turned off. Spare Construct and Spare Studio both need them.

features.name: Get updates without losing work
features.does: Get app updates without losing anything I was doing.

parts.name: Update delivery
parts.what: Update checks and safe reloads that keep unsaved work.

parts.name: Update channels
parts.what: Stable, preview and long-support channels, with pause, skip, pinned versions and roll back. Spare Construct, Spare Studio and Spare OS need them.

features.name: Find the apps in phone app stores
features.does: Find Spareware apps in the phone app stores.

parts.name: App store rules
parts.what: Meets each store's rules on payments, privacy labels and reviews.

features.name: Share a short link or QR code
features.does: Share a short link or QR code to a listing, a form or an invite, and see how many times it was opened.

parts.name: Short links and QR codes
parts.what: Short links and QR codes that open the right screen through deep links and count scans in totals only, without tracking anyone.

features.name: Find any command
features.does: Type to find and run any command, and use the shortcuts I already know.

parts.name: Command search and shortcuts
parts.what: Type to find and run any command, with shortcut sets that start from the ones people already know and can be changed, exported and shared. Spare Construct, Spare Studio, Spare Office and Spare OS need the same.

features.name: Use a work app safely on the road
features.does: Use a worker app in a car or on a bike without typing or tapping while moving.

parts.name: Phone rules on the road
parts.what: What each country's road rules allow for phones in cradles in cars and on bikes, e-bikes and scooters, starting with New Zealand's, with sources, checked against each worker screen. Spare Ride and Spare Food both need it.

parts.name: Driving-safe mode
parts.what: Worker screens that block typing while moving, use large targets, and read offers and messages aloud. Spare Food and Spare Ride both need it.

areas.name: Help and member support
areas.summary: Help pages in every language, support tied to the job, urgent help at any hour, members helping members, and a way to complain about the co-op itself, with response times published. Proposed as svc-support (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Find help myself
features.does: Search help pages for any app in my language.

parts.name: Help centre
parts.what: Articles for each app and language, searchable and linked from each screen.

parts.name: Plain-words glossary
parts.what: Explains legal and trade terms in plain words, linked wherever they appear. Spare Home and Spare Rent both need it.

features.name: Contact support about a job
features.does: Ask for help about a particular order and follow the case.

parts.name: Support cases
parts.what: Cases linked to orders and accounts, with status and replies.

parts.name: Support console
parts.what: A case queue for support staff with history, reply templates and every action logged.

features.name: Reach a person when it is urgent
features.does: Reach a person quickly about safety or money problems.

parts.name: Urgent route
parts.what: The one urgent route and on-call roster for safety and money problems, with a safety lane staffed by trained responders.

features.name: Get help another way
features.does: Get support by phone, email or the relay service if apps are hard for me to use.

parts.name: Other support channels
parts.what: Email and phone channels, and each country's relay service for Deaf, hard of hearing and speech-impaired members (example: New Zealand Relay).

features.name: Know if something is down
features.does: Check whether an app is working and when it will be fixed.

parts.name: Status page
parts.what: Live status for each app with incident updates, hosted apart from the main servers.

features.name: Help each other
features.does: Ask and answer questions with other members in a forum.

parts.name: Member forum
parts.what: A forum for each app, looked after by member moderators.

features.name: Suggest an improvement
features.does: Suggest a change, and turn it into a proposal if others support it.

parts.name: Suggestions
parts.what: Suggestions that can move to a member proposal.

features.name: See how fast support answers
features.does: See published support response times.

parts.name: Support figures
parts.what: Published response times and satisfaction for each app, through the public reporting pipeline.

features.name: Complain about the co-op itself
features.does: Make a complaint about the co-op, not just about a job, and know where to take it if I am not satisfied.

parts.name: Dispute resolution scheme
parts.what: Whether the co-op must register as a financial service provider in each country and, if so, join an approved dispute resolution scheme (example: New Zealand's Financial Service Providers Register).

parts.name: Complaints about the co-op
parts.what: A published complaints process about the co-op itself, with response times and the outside route that applies.

features.name: Get an interpreter
features.does: Have an interpreter, including sign language such as New Zealand Sign Language, for a dispute, a panel hearing or a support call.

parts.name: Interpreters
parts.what: Books qualified interpreters, including sign language such as New Zealand Sign Language, for disputes, panel hearings and support, paid at cost and shown in the ledger.

areas.name: Running it: hosting, security and admin
areas.summary: Servers run at cost by the co-op or by member groups, with monitoring, backups, encryption, signed releases, security reviews and an admin console where every action is logged. Proposed as svc-admin (KIT-A16-F10-P1).

features.name: Keep the apps running
features.does: Have apps stay up, with problems spotted and fixed quickly.

parts.name: Monitoring and alerts
parts.what: Open-source metrics, logs and alerts, with every licence checked.

parts.name: Incident response
parts.what: An on-call roster, runbooks and published incident reviews.

parts.name: Spend alerts and budgets
parts.what: Budgets and alerts on cloud and provider spend for each app, so a runaway bill is caught within hours, not at month end.

features.name: Get changes without breakage
features.does: Have changes reach members without breaking things.

parts.name: Release pipeline
parts.what: Builds, tests, staged rollouts and rollback for every service.

parts.name: Feature switches
parts.what: Turns features on for each app, region or group, with every change logged.

parts.name: Signed releases
parts.what: Signed releases, a software bill of materials, reproducible builds and app-signing keys kept offline under two-person control.

parts.name: Developer accounts and signing certificates
parts.what: Apple, Google and Windows developer accounts and code signing certificates held by the legal entity, including Google's developer verification for sideloaded Android apps from 2026 to 2027 (*unverified* dates for each country), with costs on the ledger.

parts.name: Performance budgets
parts.what: Published limits on start time, load time, memory and data use for each app, measured on old devices and real connections on every change, so a slower change does not merge. Spare Social and Spare Office both set them.

parts.name: Name and interface review
parts.what: Checks before each release that names, icons and interface designs are our own, and that other companies' names appear only to say what we replace. Spare Construct and Spare Office both map it.

features.name: Know my data is backed up
features.does: Know data survives a failure and restores are tested.

parts.name: Backups and restore drills
parts.what: Continuous off-site copies of the operation log and scheduled restore tests.

parts.name: Disaster recovery
parts.what: A second region and a tested plan to move to it.

features.name: Have servers run at cost
features.does: Have servers run at cost in the regions people use, starting with the first example country, New Zealand, with their costs fed to the ledger.

parts.name: Hosting
parts.what: Infrastructure as code for the co-op's servers in each region, starting with New Zealand.

parts.name: Hosting provider choice
parts.what: Compares hosting providers on regions in each country, starting with New Zealand, and on data sovereignty, overseas laws that can reach the data and cost, as the basis for the launch cost estimate and for where data lives.

features.name: Know the apps are secure
features.does: Know the apps are protected and checked by outside reviewers.

parts.name: Secrets and access
